headline: Duran is absent from the lineup Wednesday for Game 2 of the wild-card series against the Yankees.
story: The left-handed-hitting Duran was regularly out of the lineup versus lefty hurlers, so it's not a surprise he's sitting out as the Yankees send southpaw Max Fried to the mound. Nate Eaton will play left field, and Jahmai Jones will be Boston's designated hitter in Game 2.

headline: Nola is likely to start a potential Game 3 of the wild-card series against Atlanta on Thursday, Matt Gelb of The Athletic reports.
story: Zack Wheeler will be on three days' rest Thursday and would be available out of the bullpen, but the Phillies are likely to turn to Nola on normal rest first if they're able to force a winner-take-all contest. The 33-year-old Nola was terrific down the stretch of the regular season for Philadelphia, collecting a 2.93 ERA and 61:20 K:BB over 61.1 innings covering 11 starts from Aug. 1 on.

headline: King earned the win in Game 1 of the NL Wild Card Series against the Cubs on Tuesday. He gave up one hit with eight strikeouts and three walks over seven shutout innings.
story: The right-hander held Chicago without a hit until the seventh inning, when Nico Hoerner reached on an infield single down the third-base line. It was an electric performance from King, who threw 62 of his 97 pitches for strikes while generating 17 whiffs. The 31-year-old surrendered five runs against the Dodgers during his final start of the regular season, but it was still a productive campaign with a 3.21 ERA, 1.18 WHIP and 159:70 K:BB across 185 innings. If the Padres can win one of the next two games to push past the Cubs, King likely lines up to start Game 2 of the NLDS in Milwaukee.

headline: Bregman is starting as the designated hitter and batting second Tuesday for Game 1 of the NL Wild Card Series against the Padres.
story: Bregman will not be in the field Tuesday since it is the "safest way to make sure he gets at-bats," manager Craig Counsell said, Alden Gonzalez of ESPN.com reports. With the 32-year-old starting as the designated hitter after recently suffering multiple facial fractures, Pedro Ramirez enters the lineup as the third baseman and Michael Conforto exits to the bench.

headline: Duran (0-1) was charged with a blown save and the loss in Game 1 of the NL Wild Card Series against Atlanta on Tuesday. He allowed three runs on two hits with one strikeout and no walks over two innings.
story: Interim manager Don Mattingly called upon his closer to begin the seventh inning with the Phillies leading 3-2, and Duran delivered a clean frame on 17 pitches. The right-hander returned for the eighth and retired the first two batters he faced, but an infield single and a hit-by-pitch set the table for Austin Riley to launch a three-run homer. Duran recorded more than three outs in just one of his 61 appearances during the regular season, so the multi-inning usage by Mattingly will likely be scrutinized heavily. The Phillies are now facing elimination after having their closer throw 27 pitches in Game 1.

headline: Sale didn't factor in the decision in Game 1 of the NL Wild Card Series against the Phillies on Tuesday. He struck out nine while giving up three runs on four hits and a walk over 6.1 innings.
story: The veteran left-hander surrendered a run during the first inning but shut down Philadelphia for the next five frames before he put on two runners in the seventh that came around to score courtesy of righty reliever Didier Fuentes. Sale made just three starts in September as the club managed his workload down the stretch, and he looked plenty fresh Tuesday, touching 100 mph and throwing 95 pitches (65 strikes). Atlanta completed the comeback, and should it complete the series win, Sale would be in line to pitch in Game 2 of the NLDS against the Dodgers on Sunday.

headline: Riley went 1-for-3 with a three-run home run during Game 1 of the NL Wild Card Series against the Phillies on Tuesday.
story: The veteran third baseman came to the plate in the eighth inning with Atlanta trailing 3-2, and he delivered a three-run homer to right-center field off Philadelphia closer Jhoan Duran to flip the script. Riley closed the regular season by going 0-for-11 with six strikeouts in his last three games, dropping his OPS for the campaign to a career-worst .654 in 159 contests. Already the Game 1 hero, Riley could effectively erase all his 2026 struggles if he continues to perform in the playoffs.

headline: Chisholm is not in the lineup Tuesday for Game 1 of the AL Wild Card Series against the Red Sox.
story: The left-handed-swinging Chisholm was often held out of the lineup this season when the opposition had a tough southpaw on the bump, and Game 1 starter Payton Tolle qualifies. It will be Anthony Volpe handling second base while Chisholm begins the contest on the bench.

headline: Steele (elbow) is not on the Cubs' roster for their wild-card series versus the Padres, Meghan Montemurro of the Chicago Tribune reports.
story: Steele has been out all season while recovering from UCL revision surgery and a flexor strain. He is physically ready to pitch now, having made four rehab appearances this month, but the Cubs have decided he's not a fit for their playoff roster. Steele could earn consideration in subsequent rounds, if his team advances.

headline: Adames (elbow) has been cleared to go through his normal offseason workout routine, Justice delos Santos of The San Jose Mercury News reports.
story: Adames went down with a left (non-throwing) elbow sprain in late August, but he was ramping up workouts toward the end of the regular season and will not have any restrictions over the winter. The veteran shortstop put together a .230/.289/.424 batting line with 21 home runs over 121 games for the Giants this season.

headline: The Red Sox activated Crochet (shoulder) from the 60-day injured list Tuesday, Tim Healey of The Boston Globe reports.
story: Crochet has not appeared in a game since late April due to a strained left lat. However, the left-hander has checked off all the necessary boxes in order to convince the Red Sox he was ready for the American League Wild Card series against the Yankees. Crochet will be used in a relief role.

headline: Judge (calf) is not on the Yankees' roster for their AL Wild Card Series against the Red Sox, Jack Curry of YES Network reports.
story: Judge was diagnosed with a moderate right calf strain a little less than two weeks ago. He's made progress, having taken live batting practice Monday, but Judge has yet to try running the bases or playing the outfield since the injury. Judge will push to be ready for the ALDS, should the Yankees advance. With Judge shelved, New York will likely use Spencer Jones in right field and Trent Grisham in center field versus righties.

headline: Fantasy baseball: Which pitchers are MVPs, LVPs of 2026?
story:
Milwaukee Brewers RHP Jacob Misiorowski and New York Yankees RHP Cam Schlittler were easily the most valuable hurlers during the 2026 season for roto/categories-based leagues. The pair finishing second and third, respectively, on the overall Player Rater, behind only Chicago Cubs OF Pete Crow-Armstrong (and behind only Los Angeles Dodgers DH/SP Shohei Ohtani in points formats).

While Misiorowski and Schlittler were not among the first pitchers chosen in ESPN ADP, they didn't slip too far, going in the 10th and 14th round. It may not feel so exciting to reward them as co-MVP pitchers for fantasy baseball, but it is obvious.

Beyond that, there were myriad starting pitchers who did not go in the first half of drafts -- or even in most drafts at all -- who supplied excellent value to fantasy managers. Let's take a look at some of them.

Other MVP pitcher candidates

Parker Messick, LHP, Cleveland Guardians: Messick deserves special acknowledgement, for he went undrafted in most leagues, yet finished as a top-10 starting pitcher for both roto/categories and points formats with a 2.56 ERA in his 32 starts. Messick made seven starts during his 2025 rookie season. He was arguably the best pitching bargain of 2026.

 Drew Rasmussen, RHP, Tampa Bay Rays: After missing most of the 2023 and 2024 seasons due to injury, Rasmussen thrived in 2025. The Rays were not as cautious with his workload in 2026, as he won 16 games with a 2.67 ERA over 172 innings. He was a fantastic 13th-round pick.

Zack Wheeler, RHP, Philadelphia Phillies: Fantasy managers knew Wheeler, 36, would miss the beginning of the season recovering from thoracic outlet syndrome, so he slipped to the eighth round in ADP. Once he arrived, he rarely slipped. Wheeler made 28 starts, with a 3.00 ERA and a 1.05 WHIP. He won 14 games and struck out 193 hitters. He was a terrific value.

Gavin Williams, RHP, Guardians: Williams was a good pitcher in 2025, posting a 3.06 ERA with a strikeout per inning. While his ERA rose to 3.76 this past season, he lowered his WHIP to 1.11 and led the AL in strikeouts with 248.

 Eduardo Rodriguez, Arizona Diamondbacks: Rodriguez, 33, posted a 5.02 ERA and a 1.53 WHIP over his first two NL seasons. Little was expected from him in 2026, but then he won 16 games with a 2.89 ERA during his 32 starts. Fantastic turnaround!

Honorable mention: Cade Cavalli, Washington Nationals; Nick Martinez, Rays; Reid Detmers, Los Angeles Angels; Braxton Ashcraft, Pittsburgh Pirates; Payton Tolle, Boston Red Sox; Taj Bradley, Minnesota Twins.

Starting pitcher LVP

Garrett Crochet, Red Sox: Crochet was a first-rounder in ESPN ADP, the No. 3 pitcher after Paul Skenes and Tarik Skubal -- and he scored 41 fantasy points all season. He hit the IL in late April as a result of shoulder problems, telling reporters he wouldn't miss much time. Then he missed the remaining five months of time. Injuries happen, but this one was a big one, hurting fantasy managers more than it seemed to hinder the playoff-bound Red Sox.

Dishonorable mention: Cole Ragans, Kansas City Royals; Logan Webb, San Francisco Giants; George Kirby, Seattle Mariners; Framber Valdez, Detroit Tigers; Nick Pivetta, San Diego Padres; Luis Castillo, Mariners/Chicago White Sox.

Relief pitcher MVP

Louis Varland, Toronto Blue Jays: Varland entered his fifth MLB season with nary a save to his record, but coming off a solid 2025 season in which he emerged as a valuable relief pitcher. He further emerged as one of the best relief pitchers this past season, quickly pushing Jeff Hoffman out of the closer role, as he posted a 1.27 ERA with 35 saves, striking out 97 hitters. Relief pitching is volatile, but every so often we get a monster season like this one. Varland finished third among relief pitchers on the Player Rater, behind the Guardians' Cade Smith and Padres' Mason Miller.

Honorable mention: Bryan Baker and Kevin Kelly, Rays; Jacob Latz, Texas Rangers; Tanner Scott, Dodgers; Grant Taylor, White Sox; Mason Montgomery, Pirates; Brent Headrick, Yankees; Dylan Lee, Atlanta Braves.

Relief pitcher LVP

Edwin Diaz, Dodgers: Diaz, coming off a standout 2025 season with the New York Mets in which he posted a 1.63 ERA with 28 saves, bolted for the Dodgers with a three-year contract offer. Fantasy managers went all-in, but Diaz struggled early on, then hit the IL for months. He ultimately saved seven games, but with a horrid 8.68 ERA and 1.98 WHIP in only 18 2/3 innings. Diaz was second only to Padres star Mason Miller among relief pitchers in ESPN ADP -- a sixth-round pick -- and he scored all of 46 fantasy points.

Dishonorable mention: Andres Munoz, Mariners; Devin Williams, Mets; Bryan Abreu, Houston Astros; Jeff Hoffman, Blue Jays/Twins; Ryan Helsley, Baltimore Orioles; Daniel Palencia, Cubs; Carlos Estevez, Royals.

headline: Fantasy baseball: Which hitters are MVPs, LVPs of 2026?
story:
Fantasy managers saw what Chicago Cubs OF Pete Crow-Armstrong achieved in the first half of the 2025 season, when he was one of the top hitters in the game. Then came the final two months, as Crow-Armstrong delivered a .553 OPS with only four home runs, and it decreased his value. Crow-Armstrong still went in the sixth round of ESPN ADP for this season (No. 53), but investors could not be sure what statistics they were going to get.

What they got was the seventh 40-homer, 40-steal season in MLB history.

Crow-Armstrong started this season rather slowly, then he adjusted his mechanics and approach and, well, he became the best hitter/player in the sport. The numbers don't lie: Crow-Armstrong entered June hitting .237 with seven home runs. Then he hit .381 with 11 home runs in June and continued his assault on pitchers over the final few months. He blasted 14 home runs in August. He reached 40/40 in the closing games. This is the NL MVP -- and fantasy's MVP hitter as well.

As for the great Los Angeles Dodgers DH/SP Shohei Ohtani, it may be difficult for him to earn our nod for fantasy hitter MVP because he was the No. 1 pick in virtually every league. Monster numbers are always expected. Crow-Armstrong certainly wasn't some late-round steal (and we have some listed below), but a sixth-round choice going 40/40 is massive value. Ohtani pitched like a Cy Young Award winner for a while and the hitting numbers were there, but then he stopped pitching, struggled at the plate and ended up hitting the IL as the season approached its final weeks.

Other MVP hitter candidates

 Yordan Alvarez, DH/OF, Houston Astros: Fantasy managers did not forget that Alvarez was a terrific offensive option for four seasons prior to missing most of the 2025 campaign due to several injuries. A third-round pick in 2026 ADP, Alvarez sure bounced back and then some, delivering his best season and a likely AL MVP award. Alvarez posted career bests with 158 games, a .316 batting average, 42 home runs, 106 RBIs, 105 runs and 109 walks. He finished fifth on the overall Player Rater, third among hitters.

Jordan Walker, OF, St. Louis Cardinals: Once a top prospect, Walker hit a sad .215 with six home runs in 2025. He made changes in his approach and ended up as arguably the top bargain of 2026, considering he went undrafted (No. 458 ADP) in almost every league. He hit .269 with 29 home runs, 102 RBIs and 22 steals -- and he won the midseason Home Run Derby. Despite a tepid second half, Walker still finished 17th overall on the Rater. He should be a fantasy building block for years to come.

 Miguel Vargas, 3B/1B, Chicago White Sox: Vargas also went undrafted (No. 255 ADP) in most fantasy leagues after posting a .717 OPS with 16 home runs during the 2025 season. Then he blossomed into a legitimate star, hitting 33 home runs, scoring 106 runs and even stealing 22 bases as the White Sox made the playoffs. Vargas finished 23rd on the Rater and was fifth among hitters in points formats.

 Kevin McGonigle, SS/3B, Detroit Tigers: This talented rookie went in the Vargas range of drafts (No. 250), if he went at all in your league. What happened next? In case you didn't notice, he ended up as a top-10 hitter in points formats and No. 32 in roto/categories. Not too shabby.

 Jake McCarthy, OF, Colorado Rockies: There was little reason to invest in McCarthy prior to the season, but then he became a starter for the Rockies and delivered a top-tier outfielder season. No, really. McCarthy was the No. 7 outfielder this season -- a five-category provider in roto formats.

Honorable mention: Alec Burleson, OF/1B/DH, Cardinals; Otto Lopez, SS/2B, Miami Marlins; Sal Stewart, 1B/3B/DH, Cincinnati Reds; Luis Garcia Jr., 2B/1B/DH, New York Yankees/Washington Nationals; Jake Bauers, 1B/3B, Milwaukee Brewers; Carson Benge, OF, New York Mets.

2026's fantasy LVP hitters

 Aaron Judge, OF, Yankees: Volume matters, and Judge, the consensus No. 2 pick in ESPN leagues after Ohtani, participated in only 66 games. That's it. Fantasy managers did not get what they expected after Judge appeared in 152 and 158 games the prior two seasons. He wasn't the only top hitter to miss significant playing time due to injury (Juan Soto, Jose Ramirez, Ronald Acuna Jr.) -- it was that kind of fantasy season. Still, the good news is this: Alvarez was last season's LVP hitter (48 games) and he did OK this time around. 

Cal Raleigh, C, Seattle Mariners: Fantasy managers were warned that investing in a catcher -- any catcher -- to build a fantasy offense around is a dangerous practice. Catchers get hurt and often they play through injury and their numbers suffer as a result. After an amazing 2025 season (60 HR), Raleigh never got going in 2026, hitting just .182 with 23 home runs.

Dishonorable mention: Vladimir Guerrero Jr., 1B, Toronto Blue Jays; Francisco Lindor, SS, Mets; Gunnar Henderson, SS, Baltimore Orioles; Roman Anthony, OF, Boston Red Sox; Brent Rooker, OF/DH, Athletics.

Crow-Armstrong still went in the sixth round of ESPN ADP for this season (No. 53), but investors could not be sure what statistics they were going to get.

What they got was the seventh 40-homer, 40-steal season in MLB history.

Crow-Armstrong started this season rather slowly, then he adjusted his mechanics and approach and, well, he became the best hitter/player in the sport. The numbers don't lie: Crow-Armstrong entered June hitting .237 with seven home runs. Then he hit .381 with 11 home runs in June and continued his assault on pitchers over the final few months. He blasted 14 home runs in August. He reached 40/40 in the closing games. This is the NL MVP -- and fantasy's MVP hitter as well.

As for the great Los Angeles Dodgers DH/SP Shohei Ohtani, it may be difficult for him to earn our nod for fantasy hitter MVP because he was the No. 1 pick in virtually every league. Monster numbers are always expected. Crow-Armstrong certainly wasn't some late-round steal (and we have some listed below), but a sixth-round choice going 40/40 is massive value. Ohtani pitched like a Cy Young Award winner for a while and the hitting numbers were there, but then he stopped pitching, struggled at the plate and ended up hitting the IL as the season approached its final weeks.

Other MVP hitter candidates

 Yordan Alvarez, DH/OF, Houston Astros: Fantasy managers did not forget that Alvarez was a terrific offensive option for four seasons prior to missing most of the 2025 campaign due to several injuries. A third-round pick in 2026 ADP, Alvarez sure bounced back and then some, delivering his best season and a likely AL MVP award. Alvarez posted career bests with 158 games, a .316 batting average, 42 home runs, 106 RBIs, 105 runs and 109 walks. He finished fifth on the overall Player Rater, third among hitters.

Jordan Walker, OF, St. Louis Cardinals: Once a top prospect, Walker hit a sad .215 with six home runs in 2025. He made changes in his approach and ended up as arguably the top bargain of 2026, considering he went undrafted (No. 458 ADP) in almost every league. He hit .269 with 29 home runs, 102 RBIs and 22 steals -- and he won the midseason Home Run Derby. Despite a tepid second half, Walker still finished 17th overall on the Rater. He should be a fantasy building block for years to come.

 Miguel Vargas, 3B/1B, Chicago White Sox: Vargas also went undrafted (No. 255 ADP) in most fantasy leagues after posting a .717 OPS with 16 home runs during the 2025 season. Then he blossomed into a legitimate star, hitting 33 home runs, scoring 106 runs and even stealing 22 bases as the White Sox made the playoffs. Vargas finished 23rd on the Rater and was fifth among hitters in points formats.

 Kevin McGonigle, SS/3B, Detroit Tigers: This talented rookie went in the Vargas range of drafts (No. 250), if he went at all in your league. What happened next? In case you didn't notice, he ended up as a top-10 hitter in points formats and No. 32 in roto/categories. Not too shabby.

 Jake McCarthy, OF, Colorado Rockies: There was little reason to invest in McCarthy prior to the season, but then he became a starter for the Rockies and delivered a top-tier outfielder season. No, really. McCarthy was the No. 7 outfielder this season -- a five-category provider in roto formats.

Honorable mention: Alec Burleson, OF/1B/DH, Cardinals; Otto Lopez, SS/2B, Miami Marlins; Sal Stewart, 1B/3B/DH, Cincinnati Reds; Luis Garcia Jr., 2B/1B/DH, New York Yankees/Washington Nationals; Jake Bauers, 1B/3B, Milwaukee Brewers; Carson Benge, OF, New York Mets.

2026's fantasy LVP hitters

 Aaron Judge, OF, Yankees: Volume matters, and Judge, the consensus No. 2 pick in ESPN leagues after Ohtani, participated in only 66 games. That's it. Fantasy managers did not get what they expected after Judge appeared in 152 and 158 games the prior two seasons. He wasn't the only top hitter to miss significant playing time due to injury (Juan Soto, Jose Ramirez, Ronald Acuna Jr.) -- it was that kind of fantasy season. Still, the good news is this: Alvarez was last season's LVP hitter (48 games) and he did OK this time around. 

Cal Raleigh, C, Seattle Mariners: Fantasy managers were warned that investing in a catcher -- any catcher -- to build a fantasy offense around is a dangerous practice. Catchers get hurt and often they play through injury and their numbers suffer as a result. After an amazing 2025 season (60 HR), Raleigh never got going in 2026, hitting just .182 with 23 home runs.

Dishonorable mention: Vladimir Guerrero Jr., 1B, Toronto Blue Jays; Francisco Lindor, SS, Mets; Gunnar Henderson, SS, Baltimore Orioles; Roman Anthony, OF, Boston Red Sox; Brent Rooker, OF/DH, Athletics.

headline: Judge (calf) logged four at-bats during a live batting practice session Monday, Gary Phillips of the New York Daily News reports.
story: Phillips notes that Judge struck out once, drew a pair of walks and hit a comebacker to the pitcher during his time at the dish. While it's a positive sign that he was able to log several at-bats against live pitching, he didn't participate in any on-field running or fielding. The slugger's availability is still up in the air heading into Game 1 of the Yankees' wild-card matchup against the Red Sox. Judge hasn't appeared in a game since suffering a right calf strain Sept. 16 against Minnesota.

headline: Steele (elbow) threw a bullpen session off the mound at Petco Park on Monday, John Fanta of NBC Sports reports.
story: It remains to be seen if Steele, who has spent the season recovering from UCL revision surgery and a flexor strain, will be added to the roster for Chicago's NL Wild Card Series against the Padres. If he is added to the roster prior to Tuesday's Game 1, he would presumably be deployed out of the bullpen.

headline: Rangers president of baseball operations Chris Young said Monday that Seager could require minor offseason surgery for a bone spur in his elbow "that he's dealt with for a few months," Kennedi Landry of MLB.com reports.
story: It's not a given that Seager will choose the surgical route, but if he does, the expectation is that he will be fully recovered in time for the start of spring training. Injuries limited Seager to 102 games for the second season in a row, and he regressed at the plate year-over-year, finishing with a .227/.312/.424 batting line with 20 home runs during the 2026 campaign.

headline: Judge (calf) said Monday that he's been "feeling great" while running on an anti-gravity treadmill but has yet to try running the bases, Jorge Castillo of ESPN.com reports.
story: Judge plans to do some more running on the anti-gravity treadmill Monday and could try running outside, as well. The slugger was also scheduled to take live batting practice on the field Monday. Judge is aiming to be included on the Yankees' wild-card roster despite suffering a moderate right calf strain less than two weeks ago. If he is on the roster, it would likely be in a designated-hitter role.

headline: Burnes said Monday that the right shoulder injury which landed him on the 15-day injured list during the final weekend of the regular season was fatigue-related and he expects to be fine after rest, Steve Gilbert of MLB.com reports.
story: Burnes had his Tommy John surgery rehab interrupted by a teres major strain in June, and his season ended prematurely due to what the Diamondbacks labeled as shoulder inflammation. However, it sounds as if the veteran hurler will be able to have a normal offseason after resting for a bit. Burnes allowed nine runs with an 8:4 K:BB over 10.1 innings in three starts for Arizona in 2026.

headline: Angels interim general manager John Mozeliak said Monday that Trout approached him about playing left field and designated hitter next season, Jeff Fletcher of The Orange County Register reports.
story: Trout logged 109 starts in center field and 33 at DH in 2026, but defensive metrics were again unkind as the 35-year-old finished with a minus-5 in Outs Above Average, per Baseball Savant. The three-time American League MVP's 142 games played in 2026 marked his highest total since 2016, but he was more good than great offensively, slashing .242/.382/.421 with 22 home runs, 54 RBI and 11 steals.

headline: Yankees manager Aaron Boone said that Judge (calf) is "making progress" and will take live batting practice Monday, Brendan Kuty of The Athletic reports.
story: Judge did some hitting and throwing indoors Sunday and will hit on the field Monday. The three-time American League MVP has pledged to be ready for the wild-card matchup against the Red Sox, though the Yankees have not committed to Judge being healthy enough to be included on the roster. Judge suffered a moderate right calf strain less than two weeks ago.

headline: Orioles president of baseball operations Mike Elias said Monday that Westburg (elbow) will begin a hitting progression this week, Rich Dubroff of BaltimoreBaseball.com reports.
story: Westburg underwent Tommy John surgery in May and missed the entire 2026 season. However, because he's a position player and not a pitcher, he has a good chance to head into the 2027 season without any limitations. Westburg has slashed .264/.312/.456 over parts of three major-league seasons, and assuming health, could open next season as the Orioles' primary third baseman.

headline: Red Sox manager Chad Tracy said Monday that the team has yet to decide whether Crochet (lat) will be included on the American League Wild Card Series roster versus the Yankees, Gabrielle Starr of the Boston Herald reports.
story: Crochet has not pitched in a competitive setting since late April, as he has been brought along slowly in his recovery from a left lat strain. He's been throwing off a mound for several weeks and resumed facing hitters last week. If Crochet is included on Boston's wild-card series roster, it will be in a bullpen role, as he is not stretched out to be used as a starting pitcher.

headline: Butler went 2-for-4 in Sunday's 9-0 loss to the Astros.
story: Butler was the lone Athletics player to record multiple hits in the season finale, depositing a pair of singles. The outfielder really turned things around in the second half, slashing .280/.357/.496 with 12 homers, 40 RBI, 33 runs and four stolen bases in 66 games after the All-Star break. Overall, Butler will close 2026 with a .237/.326/.394 slash line, 17 homers, 62 RBI, 64 runs and 10 stolen bases across 154 contests.

headline: Lindor went 2-for-4 with a solo home run and an additional run scored in Sunday's 6-4 loss to the Nationals.
story: Lindor extended the Mets' lead to 4-1 in the second inning with a 409-foot shot off DJ Herz, his 21st homer this season and the 300th of his career. It's a nice way to wrap up what was otherwise a disappointing season for Lindor. He'd gone 14 games without a homer prior to Sunday, going 8-for-55 (.145) in that span. Overall, Lindor will finish an injury-shortened campaign with a .225/.309/.423 slash line, 63 runs scored, 49 RBI and three steals across 469 plate appearances.

headline: Alcantara picked up the save in Sunday's 5-3 win over Atlanta. He allowed no hits or walks while striking out one over one inning.
story: With Miami opting against having him make one last start over the weekend, Alcantara was deployed as a reliever for the third time this season in Sunday's regular-season finale. The veteran right-hander was able to work through a leadoff error and retire the next three batters in order to secure his third save. Alcantara will end the campaign with a major-league-leading 214 innings, posting a 13-11 record with a 3.87 ERA, 1.23 WHIP and 153:59 K:BB across 36 appearances (33 starts).

headline: Bregman went 4-for-4 with two home runs, a double, a walk, four RBI and three runs scored in Sunday's 6-2 win over the Red Sox.
story: Bregman was perfect at the plate, going deep in the first and third innings for his fourth multi-homer game of the second half. After struggling out of the gate this year, the veteran third baseman posted a 1.010 OPS with 19 home runs and 52 RBI over 61 games after the All-Star break. Overall, he slashed .265/.355/.464 with 28 long balls, 93 RBI, 92 runs scored and three steals across 702 plate appearances and will look to stay hot as the Cubs enter the postseason.

headline: Seager went 1-for-4 with a two-run home run in Sunday's 6-4 loss to the Twins.
story: Seager went deep in his final at-bat of the year to reach the 20-homer plateau for a fifth straight campaign. The shortstop posted an .804 OPS with 10 homers in 51 second-half games after entering the All-Star break with a lowly .666 mark. Overall, he'll wrap up his 12th major-league season slashing a disappointing .227/.312/.424 with 20 long balls, 51 RBI, 57 runs scored and two steals across 436 plate appearances.

headline: Lewis went 2-for-4 with a solo home run and a stolen base in Sunday's 6-4 win over the Rangers.
story: Lewis launched a solo shot in the eighth inning, tallying his second game with a homer and a steal this season. It was a nice end to an otherwise forgettable September in which he hit just .209 with two home runs and 11 RBI. Overall, the 27-year-old finished an inconsistent campaign slashing .227/.287/.380 with 15 long balls, 57 RBI, 51 runs scored and 16 stolen bases across 509 plate appearances.

headline: Raleigh went 3-for-5 with one RBI in Sunday's 7-3 win over the Angels.
story: Raleigh largely struggled in 2026, though he showed some signs of a turnaround late in the season. He hit .229 (19-for-83) over 22 contests in September, lifting his average for the season to .182. Raleigh added a .664 OPS, 23 home runs, 69 RBI, 49 runs scored, 15 doubles and two stolen bases over 126 contests. He failed to live up to expectations this year after finishing second in voting for AL MVP in 2025, but he should benefit from positive regression next season.

headline: Gilbert walked one over four-plus scoreless and hitless innings while striking out eight in a no-decision versus the Angels on Sunday.
story: The Mariners clearly didn't want to push Gilbert too much in a meaningless game, pulling him after he walked Moises Ballesteros to open the fifth inning, ending his chance at a perfect game. Gilbert managed just six scoreless outings this season, and only two of them came after the All-Star break as he labored down the stretch. He ends 2026 with a 12-11 record, 3.73 ERA, 1.09 WHIP and 205:49 K:BB through 186 innings over 32 starts.

headline: Walker went 2-for-3 with a solo home run, two walks and two additional runs scored in Sunday's 9-0 win over the A's.
story: Walker extended Houston's lead to 5-0 in the sixth inning with a solo shot off Scott Blewett for his 29th homer this year. The first baseman will head into the postseason on a hot streak, going 8-for-23 (.348) with four homers in his last six games. Overall, Walker slashed .226/.299/.427 across 635 regular-season plate appearances with 87 RBI and 73 runs scored.

headline: Chourio went 3-for-4 with two RBI and two runs scored in Sunday's 6-4 win over the Cardinals.
story: Chourio got a couple of rest days in the final week of the season since the Brewers were able to lock up the top spot in the National League. The outfielder had an excellent month, going 33-for-98 (.337) with 18 RBI over 24 contests in September. He ends the regular season batting .291 with an .838 OPS, 23 stolen bases and 25 homers, all personal bests. He added 75 RBI, 96 runs scored and 27 doubles over just 127 games.

headline: Harper went 1-for-5 with a solo home run in Sunday's 7-3 win over Tampa Bay.
story: Harper extended the Phillies' lead to 5-1 in the fifth inning with a solo shot off Jesse Scholtens for his 29th homer this year. Harper had been in a significant slump in the power department coming into Sunday -- he had gone deep just once in his previous 27 games. Overall, Harper will finish the regular season with a .269/.380/.485 slash line, 87 RBI and 93 runs scored across 693 plate appearances.

headline: Pasquantino went 2-for-4 with a pair of solo home runs in Sunday's 3-2 win over the Guardians.
story: Pasquantino twice gave the Royals a lead, going deep in the fifth and eighth innings. While injuries and lackluster performances defined parts of the season for Pasquantino, he finished strong with eight homers over 23 games in September. The first baseman hit .249 with a .761 OPS, 17 homers, 63 RBI, 54 runs scored, 20 doubles, two triples and five stolen bases over 114 contests in 2026.

headline: Wheeler (14-5) earned the win Sunday over Tampa Bay, allowing a run on five hits and no walks over six innings. He struck out five.
story: It was another strong outing for Wheeler, who held the Rays to just one run on Jonny DeLuca's fifth-inning homer, as the Phillies cruised to a 7-3 victory to clinch the final wild-card spot in the NL. Over his last six starts, Wheeler gave up just seven runs while striking out 45 across 37.2 innings. He'll finish the regular season with a 3.00 ERA, 1.05 WHIP and 193:47 K:BB over 28 starts (162 innings).

headline: Trout is not in the starting lineup for Sunday's game against the Mariners, Rhett Bollinger of MLB.com reports.
story: With nothing left to play for in 2026, Trout will sit having already logged 633 plate appearances this season, his most since 2016. Zach Neto will serve as the designated hitter Sunday while Oswald Peraza mans shortstop and bats seventh against right-hander Logan Gilbert.

headline: Cruz (knee) is absent from the lineup for Sunday's game versus the Tigers.
story: Cruz was forced to exit Saturday's game with a left knee injury. The good news is an MRI came back negative, per Kevin Gorman of TribLive.com, but there's no reason to push Cruz to play during the regular-season finale. He will finish the 2026 campaign having slashed .280/.368/.486 with 20 home runs and 30 stolen bases over just 97 contests.

headline: Harris is not in the lineup for Sunday's tilt in Miami.
story: Harris will receive an extra day of rest as Atlanta heads into postseason play. DaShawn Keirsey will net a start in center field during Sunday's regular-season finale.

headline: Acuna is not in the lineup for Sunday's game in Miami.
story: Sunday's regular-season finale doesn't mean anything for Atlanta as far as the postseason goes, so Acuna will get a little rest. Brewer Hicklen will patrol right field and bat eighth.

headline: Ramirez is not in the starting lineup for Sunday's game against the Royals.
story: With the Guardians' playoff seeding set after the team clinched the AL Central title Saturday, Ramirez will rest for the regular-season finale. Daniel Schneemann will start at third base and bat eighth against lefty Daniel Lynch.

headline: Smith is absent from the lineup for Sunday's contest in San Francisco.
story: Smith will get a little extra rest before the Dodgers head into postseason action. Hunter Feduccia will do the catching in Sunday's regular-season finale.

headline: Merrill is not in the lineup for Sunday's contest against the Diamondbacks.
story: Merrill will receive a little extra rest as the Padres gear up for postseason play. Jase Bowen will patrol center field and will be situated in the No. 9 spot in the Padres' batting order for Sunday's regular-season finale.

headline: Tatis is not in the lineup for Sunday's tilt versus the Diamondbacks.
story: It's the first day off since Aug. 12 for Tatis, who has been scorching hot to close out the regular season. He's slashing .337/.413/.652 with eight home runs in September. Dustin Harris will play right field, and Jake Cronenworth will cover second base for the Padres in Sunday's finale.

headline: Contreras is absent from the lineup for Sunday's game versus the Cardinals.
story: Contreras will be given an extra day of rest before the Brewers open up NLDS play next weekend. Gary Sanchez will do the catching in Sunday's regular-season finale.

headline: Contreras (hand) will serve as the designated hitter and bat third in Sunday's regular-season finale against the Cubs, Mac Cerullo of the Boston Herald reports.
story: Contreras recently expressed concern about his availability for the wild-card round after being unable to swing a bat Wednesday or Thursday. However, it now seems he's in the clear to face off against the Yankees next week, so long as he makes it through Sunday's game without a setback. Contreras leads the Red Sox in home runs (27), RBI (81) and OBP (.387) with one game to play in the regular season.

headline: Guerrero is not in the starting lineup for Sunday's game against the Reds.
story: On the heels of an AL pennant run last fall, Guerrero disappointed in a major way in 2026, with his OPS falling 160 points to .688. Recent comments about his performance and contract drew the ire of the Toronto fanbase, but he quickly walked those comments back. Charles McAdoo will draw the start at first base in the season finale.

headline: Soto (hand) is in the starting lineup for Sunday's game against the Nationals.
story: Soto was plunked on his right hand in the ninth inning Saturday, but X-rays were negative and he will tough it out for the Mets' season finale. Now a five-time All-Star, Soto has an OPS north of .900 for the fourth consecutive season, though a couple of IL stints ate into his counting stats in 2026.

headline: Tovar went 2-for-4 with a solo home run Saturday against the White Sox.
story: Tovar blasted his 13th home run of the season in the fourth inning of Saturday's win. It has been a disappointing season overall, but he has managed to end the campaign in relatively strong form with a .302 average, three homers and 13 runs scored across 19 games in September.

headline: Nola (7-12) took the loss against the Rays on Saturday, allowing three runs on four hits in one inning. He did not record a walk or a strikeout.
story: Working on two days' rest but trying to help his club make the postseason, Nola was jumped for three runs in the first inning before departing. It was a tough regular-season finale for the veteran, though he'll finish the second half with a solid 3.33 ERA over 14 starts since the All-Star break. Overall, he posted a 4.67 ERA, 1.35 WHIP and 177:59 K:BB across 175.1 innings this season and may be an option to start should the Phillies make the playoffs.

headline: Caminero went 2-for-3 with a home run, a walk, two RBI and three runs scored in Saturday's 12-1 win over the Phillies.
story: Caminero opened the scoring with a two-run blast off Aaron Nola in the first inning, reaching 100 RBI for the second straight campaign. According to Adam Berry of MLB.com, the young third baseman became just the ninth player in history to have multiple 40-homer, 100-RBI seasons within his first four years. Overall, he's slashing .277/.361/.526 with 42 long balls, 101 RBI, 100 runs scored and three steals across 700 plate appearances with one regular-season game left to play.

headline: Fantasy baseball news: Judgment day arrives for Rangers, Astros, Phillies, D-backs
story:
Everything that happens in and around MLB has some additional context when viewed from a fantasy baseball perspective. From lineup changes to minor league call-ups to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values in fantasy baseball.

Our fantasy baseball buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around MLB.

Key links: RP depth chart | Player Rater | Scoring leaders
10-day pitching forecaster | 10-day hitting forecaster

Sept. 27: Sunday's news to know

By Todd Zola

Initially, all 15 games on today's schedule were set to begin between 3:05 p.m. ET and 3:10 p.m. ET, but two games have been moved up to 1:05 p.m. ET. Neither of those changed games has any playoff ramifications. The early games are the New York Yankees hosting the Baltimore Orioles and the Washington Nationals entertaining the New York Mets. Four of the remaining 13 games do have some postseason implications. The AL West crown and the final NL wild-card spot are still undecided.

  • The Houston Astros and Texas Rangers have identical records heading into their respective Game 162s. The Astros won nine out of 13 games against the Rangers, so they hold the tiebreaker. The Astros visit the Athletics while the Rangers visit the Minnesota Twins.
  • Peter Lambert will start for the Astros. However, he threw 62 pitches last Thursday and won't be able to handle more than a few frames. Hunter Brown and Hayden Wesneski are likely unavailable, but everyone else is in play in an "all hands on deck" affair.
  • The Philadelphia Phillies hold a slim one-game lead over the Arizona Diamondbacks for the sixth seed in the National League's postseason. However, the Diamondbacks win the tiebreaker, so if the Phillies lose and the Diamondbacks win, Arizona makes the playoffs. If the Phillies win or the Diamondbacks lose, Philadelphia hits the road to play the Atlanta Braves.
  • The Diamondbacks hope that Gabriel Moreno will be in the lineup this afternoon after he was lifted from last night's game due to a hamstring issue. The club is counting on post-game treatment of the injury to allow him to play. The catcher is quietly enjoying a career season, posting an .874 OPS over 129 games.
  • Zack Wheeler is set to take the hill for the Phillies. Ideally, he'd be preparing to start Game 1 of the Wild Card Round, but the team's four-game losing streak has forced a change in plans. He'll be pitching on only four days of rest, but is coming off one of his best games of the season. Yesterday, the club announced that Jesus Luzardo will be activated from the 15-day IL and will be available out of the bullpen.
  • Chandler Simpson missed yesterday's game and is likely going to miss the season finale as well. The Tampa Bay Rays speedster will likely fall four steals short of 50. He currently leads the AL with 46, but Bobby Witt Jr. is on his tail with 45.
  • Juan Soto of the Mets is questionable for today's early matinee. He was hit in the hand by a pitch in the ninth inning of last night's affair. He'll likely undergo imaging, then the club will provide a status update.
  • The Pittsburgh Pirates could play their finale without Oneil Cruz. The breakout outfielder tweaked his knee making a catch yesterday.
  • Be sure to check out the latest fantasy lineup advice as well as the MLB betting tips for Sunday.

Sept. 26: Saturday morning's news to know

By Todd Zola

Saturday's 13-game slate gets started at 12:25 p.m. ET with the Washington Nationals hosting the New York Mets. Five matinees follow, and seven evening games close out the penultimate day of the regular season.

  • After playing a doubleheader Friday, the Boston Red Sox and Chicago Cubs will wrap up the season Sunday at Tropicana Field. The Red Sox have secured the second AL wild card, but the game could have seeding implications for the Cubs. The New York Yankees and Baltimore Orioles also moved today's game to Friday, but they're hoping to play Game 162 on Sunday in the Bronx.
  • Several teams will be patching together their pitching, starting with the Nationals in the early game. Connelly Early is set to start before Jake Irvin handles bulk innings. It will be Early's debut for the Nationals; he's expected to toss two or three innings.
  • Justin Verlander will be making the final start of his vaunted career when the Detroit Tigers host the Pittsburgh Pirates. The future Hall of Famer started one game in the opening series, then spent the rest of the season on the 60-day IL with hamstring and hip injuries. He's not expected to stay in very long, with Jack Flaherty set to replace the veteran. The Pirates will counter with Kirby Yates as opener before passing the baton to Antwone Kelly.
  • The American League West is still up for grabs with the Texas Rangers and Houston Astros tied with two games left in the regular season. The Rangers are on the road against the Minnesota Twins. Meanwhile, the Astros finish the season in Sacramento against the Athletics.
  • One playoff spot remains unsettled in the National League with the Philadelphia Phillies' lead over the Arizona Diamondbacks down to one game for the final wild-card berth. The Phillies host the Tampa Bay Rays with the Diamondbacks visiting the San Diego Padres.
  • The Rangers will likely be shorthanded against the Twins after Josh Jung was diagnosed with a broken right hand. He was hit by a pitch, almost certainly ending his regular season while putting a potential playoff appearance in jeopardy.
  • Chandler Simpson's quest for 50 stolen bases hit a speed bump. He left last night's Rays' game after fouling a ball off his foot. The AL stolen base leader remains at 46 steals.
  • The Milwaukee Brewers will be without Andrew Vaughn through the weekend after placing him on the 10-day IL with an illness. However, he'll be eligible to return when the Brewers open the NLDS.
  • The Red Sox are anticipating being without Mickey Gasper when they face the Yankees in the wild-card round. He hurt his right bicep swinging at strike three in the first game of yesterday's doubleheader.

By Todd Zola

Saturday's 13-game slate gets started at 12:25 p.m. ET with the Washington Nationals hosting the New York Mets. Five matinees follow, and seven evening games close out the penultimate day of the regular season.

  • After playing a doubleheader Friday, the Boston Red Sox and Chicago Cubs will wrap up the season Sunday at Tropicana Field. The Red Sox have secured the second AL wild card, but the game could have seeding implications for the Cubs. The New York Yankees and Baltimore Orioles also moved today's game to Friday, but they're hoping to play Game 162 on Sunday in the Bronx.

headline: Fantasy baseball news: Judgment day arrives for Rangers, Astros, Phillies, D-backs
story:
Everything that happens in and around MLB has some additional context when viewed from a fantasy baseball perspective. From lineup changes to minor league call-ups to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values in fantasy baseball.

Our fantasy baseball buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around MLB.

Key links: RP depth chart | Player Rater | Scoring leaders
10-day pitching forecaster | 10-day hitting forecaster

Sept. 27: Sunday's news to know

By Todd Zola

Initially, all 15 games on today's schedule were set to begin between 3:05 p.m. ET and 3:10 p.m. ET, but two games have been moved up to 1:05 p.m. ET. Neither of those changed games has any playoff ramifications. The early games are the New York Yankees hosting the Baltimore Orioles and the Washington Nationals entertaining the New York Mets. Four of the remaining 13 games do have some postseason implications. The AL West crown and the final NL wild-card spot are still undecided.

  • The Houston Astros and Texas Rangers have identical records heading into their respective Game 162s. The Astros won nine out of 13 games against the Rangers, so they hold the tiebreaker. The Astros visit the Athletics while the Rangers visit the Minnesota Twins.
  • Peter Lambert will start for the Astros. However, he threw 62 pitches last Thursday and won't be able to handle more than a few frames. Hunter Brown and Hayden Wesneski are likely unavailable, but everyone else is in play in an "all hands on deck" affair.
  • The Philadelphia Phillies hold a slim one-game lead over the Arizona Diamondbacks for the sixth seed in the National League's postseason. However, the Diamondbacks win the tiebreaker, so if the Phillies lose and the Diamondbacks win, Arizona makes the playoffs. If the Phillies win or the Diamondbacks lose, Philadelphia hits the road to play the Atlanta Braves.
  • The Diamondbacks hope that Gabriel Moreno will be in the lineup this afternoon after he was lifted from last night's game due to a hamstring issue. The club is counting on post-game treatment of the injury to allow him to play. The catcher is quietly enjoying a career season, posting an .874 OPS over 129 games.
  • Zack Wheeler is set to take the hill for the Phillies. Ideally, he'd be preparing to start Game 1 of the Wild Card Round, but the team's four-game losing streak has forced a change in plans. He'll be pitching on only four days of rest, but is coming off one of his best games of the season. Yesterday, the club announced that Jesus Luzardo will be activated from the 15-day IL and will be available out of the bullpen.
  • Chandler Simpson missed yesterday's game and is likely going to miss the season finale as well. The Tampa Bay Rays speedster will likely fall four steals short of 50. He currently leads the AL with 46, but Bobby Witt Jr. is on his tail with 45.
  • Juan Soto of the Mets is questionable for today's early matinee. He was hit in the hand by a pitch in the ninth inning of last night's affair. He'll likely undergo imaging, then the club will provide a status update.
  • The Pittsburgh Pirates could play their finale without Oneil Cruz. The breakout outfielder tweaked his knee making a catch yesterday.
  • Be sure to check out the latest fantasy lineup advice as well as the MLB betting tips for Sunday.

headline: Naylor went 0-for-4 with a walk, one RBI and a stolen base in Saturday's 8-4 win over the Angels.
story: Naylor has reached the 30-steal mark for the second year in a row. That's a rare accomplishment for a first baseman -- he's the first to post 30 steals in consecutive years since George Sisler did in three straight years from 1920-1922. Prior to Naylor's last two years, the last first baseman to have 30 steals in a campaign was Paul Goldschmidt in 2016. While the work on the basepaths has been impressive, Naylor has struggled in other areas, batting .261 with a .667 OPS, 10 home runs, 56 RBI, 48 runs scored and 22 doubles over 151 contests. That OPS is his lowest in a full-length campaign; only his .621 mark in the abbreviated 2020 campaign is worse in his eight seasons.

headline: Alvarez went 2-for-5 with a three-run home run, a double and a second run scored in Saturday's 13-2 win over the Athletics.
story: Alvarez's blast was his 42nd of the season, putting him one back of Pete Alonso for the American League lead. Over the last 11 games, Alvarez has gone 16-for-40 (.400) with four homers and nine RBI. The star slugger leads the majors in batting average (.316) and OPS (1.036) this year while adding 105 RBI, 104 runs scored, 34 doubles, one triple and one stolen base over 157 contests in the best season of his career by most metrics.

headline: Merrill went 2-for-4 with a walk, one RBI, a stolen base and two runs scored in Saturday's 10-7 win over the Diamondbacks.
story: Merrill ended a stretch of eight games without a multi-hit effort, a span in which he hit .200 with three extra-base hits. The outfielder hadn't stolen a base since Sept. 11 versus the Giants. Merrill has generally found success on the basepaths this season, going 27-for-31 on steal attempts. He's added 26 home runs, 87 RBI, 86 runs scored, 26 doubles and five triples while batting .254 with a .743 OPS across a career-high 158 games in his third campaign in the majors.

headline: Machado went 2-for-5 with a three-run home run in Saturday's 10-7 win over the Diamondbacks.
story: Machado reached the 30-homer mark for the first time since 2023 when he went deep in the fourth inning. The third baseman has left the yard six times and added 15 RBI over his last 20 contests despite batting just .195 (15-for-77) in that span. He's hitting .216 with a .710 OPS, 90 RBI, 82 runs scored, 22 doubles and five stolen bases over 157 contests this season.

headline: Wheeler will be the Phillies' starter for Sunday's regular-season finale against the Rays, Mark Bowman of MLB.com reports.
story: The Phillies were unable to clinch a wild-card spot for the playoffs following Saturday's loss to the Rays. As a result, Wheeler will take to the mound for Sunday's regular-season finale, meaning that he wouldn't be available to pitch in the playoffs until Game 3 of the NL Wild Card Series, if Philadelphia qualifies. Jesus Luzardo (shoulder) is also expected to be activated from the 15-day IL ahead of Sunday's game and be available out of the bullpen.

headline: Witt went 2-for-4 with two runs scored and a stolen base in Saturday's 11-5 loss to the Guardians.
story: Witt stole second base and came around to score in the first inning before scoring another run in the eighth. The superstar has hit safely in each of his past eight contests, swiping three bags and crossing the plate 10 times in that span. For the year, he's slashing .283/.361/.444 with 18 homers, 54 RBI, 94 runs scored and 45 steals across 628 plate appearances.

headline: Ober (7-7) took the loss Saturday against Texas, striking out five while allowing six runs on 10 hits and one walk in five innings.
story: Most of the damage came in the second inning, when the Rangers plated four runs. Ober opened the season as part of the Minnesota rotation but may have to battle for a starting role next year -- he posted just two quality starts in 13 outings after coming off the injured list in early July. He'll finish the campaign with a 4.47 ERA, 1.30 WHIP and 96:37 K:BB over 131 innings.

headline: Harris went 4-for-5 with a pair of doubles, one RBI and three runs scored in an 8-3 win over Miami on Saturday.
story: After a slow start to the month of September, Harris is heating up just in time for the postseason, The center fielder has picked up multiple hits in seven of his last 13 games, while two of his four-hit tallies on the year have come during that span. He's hitting .294 with a career-high 26 homers, 36 doubles, 87 RBI, 12 stolen bases and 79 runs scored over 591 at-bats in a bounce-back campaign.

headline: Snell took a no-decision Saturday against the Giants, allowing one run on five hits and no walks in four innings. He struck out three.
story: Snell experienced left groin tightness during his most recent start in Cincinnati, but he looked healthy in a tune-up start Saturday ahead of the playoffs. The southpaw missed a big chunk of the year due to shoulder and elbow issues, which limited him to nine starts, but he yielded fewer than two runs each time out besides his first outing way back on May 9. He's rolling into the postseason with a 1.90 ERA, 1.10 WHIP and 55:16 K:BB over 42.2 regular-season innings.

headline: Nola will start Saturday's game against the Rays, Matt Gelb of The Athletic reports.
story: The Phillies will send Nola back to the mound Saturday after just two days' rest as they look to clinch the final wild-card spot in the National League. Because the 33-year-old just threw six innings Wednesday against the Brewers, the Phillies will likely limit him to around two or three innings Saturday before turning things over to their bullpen.

headline: Soto was removed from Saturday's game against the Nationals after getting hit on the hand by a pitch, Anthony DiComo of MLB.com reports.
story: Soto was taken out of the game immediately after taking a 91.7-mph sinker off his right hand in the ninth inning. The Mets will likely send him in for imaging and should provide an update on his status in the near future, but with just one game left in the season and the Mets out of the playoff picture, he may sit out New York's season finale if he's still feeling sore Sunday.

headline: Cruz was removed from Saturday's game against the Tigers due to an apparent injury, Dominic Campbell of SI.com reports.
story: Cruz's knee seemed to be bothering him after his foot got stuck in the grass while he made a sliding catch in the first inning, and he was eventually taken out of the game in the third. The Pirates should provide more information on his status in the near future, but with just one game left on the schedule after Saturday, Pittsburgh may opt to keep him on the sidelines no matter what.

headline: Freeman isn't in the lineup for Saturday's game against the Giants.
story: Freeman will get a chance to regroup Saturday after turning in just a .522 OPS in 45 plate appearances while starting each of the Dodgers' last 10 games. Enrique Hernandez will start at first base and bat eighth while Freeman sits.

headline: Fantasy baseball lineup advice: Kade Anderson tops streaming candidates on penultimate day of the season
story:
Check out all of our starting pitcher rankings and other lineup selection tools here to help you make smart fantasy baseball lineup decisions. All fantasy advice is geared toward ESPN 10-team leagues with standard scoring.

Note: All information is accurate as of the time of publication. For updates, as well as any breaking news that might impact today's MLB slate, be sure to check out the latest fantasy baseball buzz. 

Other resources:  RP depth chart | 2026 Rankings 
ESPN's 2026 Player Rater | Betting notes for Saturday

Pitchers to stream on Saturday

  • Kade Anderson has compiled 125 1/3 innings between the minors and majors, so he should pitch his finale with no restrictions, logging his usual 85 or so pitches. Last time out, that was enough to get him through seven shutout innings in Coors Field, where he fanned seven with no walks. Expecting a repeat is aggressive, but there is a chance with a home matchup against the Los Angeles Angels.
  • In rotisserie and category head-to-head, this weekend is all about category management. It comes with some baggage, but Jonah Tong heads the list for those needing strikeouts. The New York Mets end the season on the road against the Washington Nationals. Over the course of the season, the Nationals have generally put the ball in play, but they have fanned at a higher clip this month, and lineups during the final weekend don't usually reflect the best the team can offer.
  • Back to the Angels-Mariners matchup, Ryan Johnson is another option for punchouts, and he has better control than Tong. Not only that, the Mariners are also fanning more in September. Johnson has 24 strikeouts with just three walks over his last 22 2/3 frames.

Hitters to stream on Saturday

  • Chandler Simpson enters Friday's action with 46 stolen bases. Players like to chase round numbers, so Simpson will try to reach 50 bags when the Tampa Bay Rays visit the Philadelphia Phillies. Jonathan Aranda is also in play, especially if the Rays face a right-hander.
  • Teoscar Hernandez sports a .920 OPS against left-handed pitching this season, and the Los Angeles Dodgers are on the road against the San Francisco Giants and lefty Matt Wilkinson. The Dodgers will likely play their regulars Saturday and then give them a rest while they wait for the NLDS next week.
  • Sam Antonacci likely won't win the AL Rookie of the Year, but he'll be in the conversation. The Chicago White Sox are still playing for the AL Central title, so the leadoff hitter will likely get five chances to produce, the first facing Ryan Feltner, followed by a suspect Colorado Rockies bullpen.
  • Travis Bazzana is the Cleveland Guardians' counterpart to Antonacci. The Australian-born infielder is having a fine rookie season, batting atop the order. He's especially productive against right-handers, and the Kansas City Royals are slated to send Michael Wacha to the Kauffman Stadium mound.

headline: Semien isn't in the lineup for Saturday's game against Washington.
story: Semien will step out of the starting nine Saturday after going just 1-for-19 across New York's last five games. Ronny Mauricio will replace him at second base and bat ninth.

headline: Brown (6-4) took the loss Friday against the A's after allowing two runs (one earned) on two hits and four walks while striking out four over 5.1 innings.
story: Brown carried a 1-0 lead into the sixth inning, but a fielding error by Jose Altuve sparked the Athletics' comeback. Brown departed after a sacrifice bunt put runners at second and third with one out, and Bennett Sousa immediately surrendered a two-run single to Michael Stefanic, adding two runs to Brown's line. Brown otherwise held the Athletics to two hits, but his four walks raised his pitch count and kept him from working deeper into the game. Even though this outing didn't end as Brown or the Astros would've wanted, he ended the regular season on a strong note, allowing two earned runs or fewer in seven of his last eight starts, and just two over his last 15.1 frames. He posted a 3.19 ERA in 20 starts and 107.1 innings, marking his third straight regular season with an ERA below 3.50.

headline: DeGrom (11-11) took the loss Friday against the Twins after allowing eight runs on eight hits and three walks while striking out five over four innings.
story: DeGrom matched a season high in runs allowed at the worst possible time, as the Rangers are in a tight race in the AL West. The subpar outing overshadowed the fact that the star hurler recorded his 200th strikeout of the season Friday, reaching the milestone for the first time since 2019. DeGrom made 31 starts this season and has pitched at least 160 innings in back-to-back years for the first time since 2018-19. He finishes the regular season with a 4.20 ERA and 1.14 WHIP across 162.2 frames. If the Rangers make the playoffs, expect deGrom to take the ball in the AL Wild Card Series.

headline: Perez went 1-for-4 with a two-run homer and a walk during Friday's 12-9 loss to the Guardians.
story: Perez launched a homer in his second consecutive game Friday. The 36-year-old belted a two-run shot in the ninth inning off Matt Festa to cut into the lead. After Friday's performance, Perez is slashing .229/.273/.382 with 21 homers and 77 RBI in 620 plate appearances this season.

headline: Miller (4-10) allowed five runs on six hits and two walks while striking out seven over six innings to take the loss Friday versus the Angels.
story: Miller had a decent start going through five innings before Christian Moore tagged him for a three-run home run in the sixth. Miller's campaign was a tale of two halves -- he had a 1.71 ERA over his first nine outings, but he went winless (0-8) over his last 13 games, posting a 6.14 ERA across 66 innings in that span. It shakes out as a 4.17 ERA overall, along with a 1.16 WHIP and 119:38 K:BB across 118.2 innings through 22 games (21 starts). The silver linings were Miller improving his strikeout, walk and home run rates from last year while staying healthy after opening the year with an oblique strain.

headline: Smith went 3-for-4 in Friday's 2-0 win over the Giants.
story: Smith's trio of singles Friday accounted for his third multi-hit effort over his last seven games. The catcher is batting .458 (11-for-24) in that span. For the season, he's hitting .259 with a .782 OPS, 10 home runs, 34 RBI, 34 runs scored, nine doubles and no stolen bases over 72 contests.

headline: Hernandez went 1-for-4 with a solo home run in Friday's 2-0 win over the Giants.
story: Hernandez's six-game hitting streak ended Thursday, but he bounced back with a homer in his first at-bat Friday. That blast was all the Dodgers needed to get this win. Hernandez is now batting .268 with a .763 OPS, 16 long balls, 64 RBI, 66 runs scored, 17 doubles, two triples and five stolen bases over 123 games. In September, he's hitting .354 with a .997 OPS, getting hot at just the right time.

headline: Skubal (12-7) pitched seven shutout innings Friday, allowing just three hits and striking out 10 without walking a batter to earn the win over the Giants.
story: Skubal struggled against the Giants last week, but he bounced right back in his last start of the regular season. He likely could have kept going -- he exited at 75 pitches (60 strikes), but the Dodgers have no need to take unnecessary risks on the eve of the postseason. Skubal ends the regular season with a 2.72 ERA, 0.96 WHIP and 186:27 K:BB over 158.2 innings across 26 starts between the Dodgers and the Tigers. He'll likely make a start during the NLDS on more than one week of rest.

headline: Crews went 1-for-3 with a solo home run, two steals and two additional runs scored during the Nationals' 7-6 win over the Mets on Friday.
story: It was the second time in three games that Crews logged two steals, and his solo homer in the seventh ended up being the game-winning run for the Nationals. The 24-year-old outfielder is slashing .224/.290/.375 with 13 steals, 13 home runs, 44 RBI and 54 runs scored across 435 plate appearances this season.

headline: Bichette went 2-for-4 with an RBI double and a solo home run during the Mets' 7-6 loss to the Nationals on Friday.
story: Bichette tied things up at 2-2 with an RBI double in the third inning before adding a solo homer in the fifth. It was his first multi-hit game since Sept. 15 against the Orioles and 43rd of the season. He's also up to 18 home runs, matching his total from the 2025 regular season with the Blue Jays, though his 2026 slash line of .261/.312/.393 is noticeably lower than last year (.311/.357/.483).

headline: De La Cruz went 1-for-4 with a two-run double and a steal during the Reds' 6-5 loss to the Blue Jays on Friday.
story: De La Cruz smacked his 30th home run of the season in a 7-6 win over Atlanta on Thursday, and he swiped his 30th bag of the season one day later in Toronto. In doing so, he became the fourth player in franchise history to record 30 homers and 30 steals in a season, with Brandon Phillips most recently joining the club in 2007. De La Cruz ranks in the top-10 in the majors this season in both slugging percentage (.521) and OPS (.888) across 627 plate appearances.

headline: Alonso went 4-for-8 with two home runs, two walks, three RBI and four runs scored across both games of Friday's doubleheader against the Yankees.
story: Alonso took sole possession of the American League lead in home runs with two long balls in the matinee before reaching base three times in the nightcap. Prior to his single in the fourth inning of the first game, the slugger's previous seven hits had left the yard. He's gone deep 11 times overall in 23 September contests and is slashing .267/.363/.522 with 43 homers, 113 RBI, 100 runs scored and five steals across 700 plate appearances, with one game to go this season.

headline: Peralta (10-11) earned the win against the Phillies on Friday, allowing four hits and three walks while striking out four across 5.1 scoreless innings.
story: Peralta lost six of 11 starts from June 20 to August 21, but the veteran right-hander ended the regular season strongly with five wins over his last six outings. Friday's outing was his fifth start in which he gave up zero earned runs while tossing five or more innings, and he generated 12 whiffs and seven groundouts in the outing. He'll finish the regular season with a 4.42 ERA, 1.33 WHIP and 156:63 K:BB over 169 innings between the Mets and Rays. Tampa Bay will enter the playoffs as the AL's top seed, so Peralta will get some rest before toeing the rubber for the ALDS.

headline: The Mariners placed Munoz on the 15-day injured list Friday with right knee inflammation.
story: Munoz hasn't pitched since Sunday due to knee problems, and although MRI results on his knee came back negative Tuesday, the Mariners will play it safe and shut their closer down for the year. The 27-year-old didn't quite live up to expectations this season, posting a 4.24 ERA and 1.22 WHIP across 57.1 innings, but he still managed to turn in 28 saves and an 89:24 K:BB. Troy Taylor was called up from Triple-A in a corresponding move.

headline: Raleigh is not in the starting lineup for Friday's game against the Angels.
story: Jhonny Pereda will step in behind the plate to catch for starter Bryce Miller, as Raleigh sits amid an 0-for-12 stretch. Raleigh is wrapping up one of the most disappointing follow-ups to an MVP-caliber season in recent memory, as he's slashing just .179/.294/.369 across 520 plate appearances in 2026.

headline: Chourio isn't in the lineup for Friday's game against the Cardinals.
story: Chourio will get another chance to rest Friday after coming off the bench and going 1-for-1 with a solo homer, a walk, an additional run scored and a steal Thursday against the Phillies. Sal Frelick, Garrett Mitchell and Luis Lara will start across the outfield while Chourio sits.

headline: Cease (shoulder) said Friday that he anticipates having a relatively normal offseason, Arden Zwelling of Sportsnet.ca reports.
story: Surgery was ruled out, but Cease will get some downtime over the next several weeks to allow the inflammation in his shoulder to subside. He still expects to be ready for the start of spring training in 2027. A Cy Young candidate throughout much of the campaign, Cease finishes the 2026 season with a 2.40 ERA, 1.10 WHIP and 239 strikeouts across 29 starts and 169 innings.

headline: Santander (shoulder) will not be returning to the Blue Jays this season, Arden Zwelling of Sportsnet.ca reports.
story: Santander had been working his way back from left shoulder surgery, advancing to a rehab assignment earlier this month. However, he had a back issue crop up during his assignment, and the Blue Jays ultimately decided to have him get an early start on his offseason training. Santander did not make a single big-league appearance this season and has totaled just 54 regular-season games played in his first two years with Toronto.

headline: Bregman is absent from the lineup for the second game of Friday's doubleheader in Boston.
story: After missing three contests with multiple facial fractures, Bregman returned to action for the first game of the twin bill, going 0-for-4 with a strikeout. Matt Shaw will fill in at third base for the Cubs in Friday's nightcap.

headline: The Diamondbacks placed Burnes on the 15-day injured list Friday with right shoulder inflammation.
story: Burnes showed diminished velocity in his last start versus the Yankees, and he served up three home runs during a four-batter span at one point. The veteran righty had a setback in his recovery from Tommy John surgery earlier this season when he suffered a teres major strain, though there's no indication at this point that the new injury is related. It's unclear whether Burnes has a chance to pitch at some point in the postseason, should the Diamondbacks qualify. Burnes had been slated to start Saturday's game in San Diego, but that assignment could now go to Ryne Nelson.

headline: McLain is not in the lineup for Friday's contest in Toronto.
story: McLain had started each of the last nine games, but he will begin Friday's festivities on the bench. Juan Brito will handle second base for the Reds, and he'll be situated in the No. 7 slot in the batting order.

headline: Chisholm is not in the lineup for the first game of Friday's doubleheader versus the Orioles.
story: Chisholm will rest up during the first game before likely returning to the Yankees' lineup during the nightcap. It will be Jose Caballero handling second base and batting ninth during Friday's matinee.

headline: Bellinger is absent from the lineup for the first game of Friday's doubleheader against the Orioles.
story: Bellinger will rest during Friday's afternoon contest, but he will likely be back in there for the second game of the twin bill. Heliot Ramos is handling left field for the Yankees in the first game.

headline: Happ is not in the lineup for the first game of Friday's doubleheader in Boston.
story: Happ is likely to be back in there for the second game of the twin bill, but he'll begin the first tilt on the bench. Tyrone Taylor will play left field and will bat cleanup for the Cubs.

headline: Bregman (face) will start at designated hitter and bat third in the first game of Friday's doubleheader in Boston.
story: Bregman sustained multiple facial fractures and a swollen left eye after being struck by a ball while in the on-deck circle during Sunday's game against the Reds. He did not require surgery, however, and the 32-year-old has made a rapid recovery to return to the Cubs' lineup as he gets ramped back up ahead of the postseason.

story:

Pitchers to stream on Friday

  • Andrew Alvarez hopes to carry his late-season momentum into next year. He's been dominant over his past four outings, posting a 1.16 ERA and 0.94 WHIP with 27 strikeouts over 23 1/3 innings, albeit with a generous 10 walks. The Washington Nationals end the season with a home series against the New York Mets, whose offense sports the fourth-lowest wOBA facing left-handers over the last month.
  • Robert Gasser has two reasons to end the regular season on a high note. The first is that the Milwaukee Brewers have not yet clinched the top seed in the National League, and the other is that he's pitching for a spot in the postseason rotation. Allowing just one earned run in 12 innings over his previous two starts has Gasser in the mix with Shane Drohan and Kyle Harrison. The Brewers are home against the St. Louis Cardinals, whose second-half fade has them looking to next season. Part of their struggles is a spike in strikeouts facing lefties since the break.
  • Jackson Jobe is enjoying a strong September with a 3.12 ERA and 0.87 WHIP over his first three outings, fanning 24 with just four walks over 17 frames. The Detroit Tigers host the Pittsburgh Pirates to close out the year. Jobe faces an offense that has produced against right-handers all season, but they also offer strikeout upside and Jobe has been dominant recently.
  • Injury frustration aside, Bryce Miller has pitched well this season, as opposed to others in the vaunted Seattle Mariners' rotation. The club is hanging onto slim playoff aspirations when they entertain the Los Angeles Angels. Control issues have haunted Miller down the stretch, but the Angels are one of the league's least-patient teams, while striking out at an elevated clip.

Hitters to stream on Friday

  • With the Houston Astros still in the playoff mix, Yainer Diaz and Cam Smith are two of the best streaming targets. They both enjoy the platoon edge in Sacramento against Jacob Lopez and the Athletics. While Sutter Health Park won't play as small compared to the summer months, the game-time temperature is forecast to be 80 degrees with a slight wind blowing out.
  • Last season's American League champions are just playing for pride when the Toronto Blue Jays host the Cincinnati Reds. Even so, Alejandro Kirk and Kazuma Okamoto are solid options for power when they face lefty Nick Lodolo, who has surrendered 20 long balls in only 103 2/3 innings.

Hitters to avoid on Friday

  • Usually, picking up hitters for a doubleheader is a great way to amass extra counting stats. An exception is the Fenway Park twin bill between the Boston Red Sox and Chicago Cubs. There is a chance the second game isn't played with the impending Nor'easter, and the wind is forecast to be blowing in around 25 mph for the opener and nightcap.

headline: Betts went 3-for-5 with a double, a walk and a run scored in Thursday's 4-2 loss to the Padres.
story: Betts has gone 14-for-28 (.500) with four multi-hit efforts over his last seven games. He's added two home runs, five doubles and six RBI in that span. With another late-season surge under his belt, Betts looks playoff ready. He's batting .261 with a .784 OPS, 22 home runs, 68 RBI, 70 runs scored, 25 doubles and two stolen bases across 120 contests this season.

headline: Glasnow (5-2) allowed three runs on three hits and two walks while striking out 11 over 6.1 innings to take the loss versus the Padres on Thursday.
story: Glasnow gave up one run in the sixth inning and then left two runners on base in the seventh, both of whom scored after Justin Wrobleski took over on the mound. Despite the loss, it was another strong start for Glasnow, who has racked up double-digit strikeouts in his last two starts. He ends the regular season with a 3.53 ERA, 0.95 WHIP and 98:25 K:BB across 74 innings over 13 starts. Glasnow will get a little extra rest before a potential start during the NLDS.

headline: Tatis went 2-for-3 with a walk, one RBI and two stolen bases in Thursday's 4-2 win over the Dodgers.
story: Tatis is up to 38 steals this season, including seven over his last 16 games. He's also batting .369 (24-for-65) with eight extra-base hits in that span. If Tatis keeps running over the weekend against the Diamondbacks, he'll have a chance to reach 40 steals for the first time. He's batting .289 with an .828 OPS, 25 home runs, 82 RBI, 95 runs scored, 31 doubles and three triples over 157 contests this year.

headline: Miller allowed a run on one hit and struck out two over one inning to earn the save in Thursday's 4-2 win over the Dodgers.
story: Miller gave up an RBI double to Shohei Ohtani but was able to preserve the Padres' lead. Miller has given up just 13 runs all season (10 earned), but he's allowed six runs (five earned) over his last 13.2 innings dating back to Aug. 25. The star closer has a 1.30 ERA, 0.84 WHIP and 127:24 K:BB through 69 innings while converting 38 of 41 save chances, but he's not in the best form as the Padres look to lock up a playoff spot.

headline: Rodriguez went 2-for-4 with a two-run home run in Thursday's 6-4 loss to the Angels.
story: Rodriguez went deep in the second inning to put the Mariners ahead temporarily. He had gone 11 games without a long ball, though he batted .364 in that span. For the season, the star outfielder is batting .250 with a .718 OPS, 22 homers, 70 RBI, 69 runs scored, 26 doubles and 22 stolen bases over 148 contests in what's been the most challenging campaign of his career.

headline: Butler went 3-for-5 with a double in Thursday's 7-5 loss to the Astros.
story: Butler wasn't able to join in on the run production, but he put up a third straight multi-hit effort. The outfielder has gone 17-for-47 (.362) over his last 12 contests. He's batting .239 with a .727 OPS, 17 home runs, 61 RBI, 63 runs scored, 19 doubles, two triples and 10 stolen bases over 151 games this season.

headline: Walker went 2-for-4 with a solo home run and a second run scored in Thursday's 7-5 win over the Athletics.
story: Walker has reclaimed some power this week, going yard twice over his last three games. He is 6-for-20 (.300) across his last five contests after a brutal 0-for-20 stretch from Sept. 11-18. The first baseman is batting .223 with a .710 OPS, 27 homers, 84 RBI, 69 runs scored, 25 doubles and one triple across 153 games this season.

headline: Contreras (hand) expressed concern Thursday about his availability for Game 1 of the AL Wild Card Series next week, Ian Browne of MLB.com reports. "I'm working hard with the trainers, the hand is slowly getting better," Contreras said. "But I haven't been able to swing the last two days. I'll be honest with the team. I know Tuesday is a really important game. It's a really important series, and I'll be completely honest with the team."
