Canzone was starting to figure out lefties this year, batting .275/.453/.600 with four homers against them in 53 trips to the plate. He deserves better than to have his daily matchups nitpicked. Alas, it seems to be a likely outcome, meaning he'll become more of a "must start against righties" player best used in daily formats like ESPN's.

Neither of the prospects is particularly close to being major league ready, nor is either highly regarded. Hoppe, for his part, should help the Orioles as a middle reliever.

Philadelphia Phillies trade for 1B/2B/DH Luis Arraez and RP Caleb Killian

Karabell (Aug. 3): Desperate for offensive aid and a setup reliever, the Phillies achieve these objectives in a trade with the San Francisco Giants for prospects. The nomadic Arraez, a three-time batting champion (and with three different franchises), joins his fifth team in the past five seasons. Arraez is one of the most unique players in baseball, as what he lacks in power he makes up for with extreme contact. Only 13 hitters boast more fantasy points this season. Arraez, a career .318 hitter, is already a points-league star and this trade aids his value.

Not known for his defensive prowess, Arraez has played a surprisingly excellent second base this season. However, Bryson Stott handles second base in Philadelphia. The Phillies may make room by moving a willing Bryce Harper back to the outfield, which he hasn't played since 2022. They may move Stott to third base, and Alec Bohm to first. Perhaps another trade is pending. The DH spot is capably filled by Kyle Schwarber. Regardless, expect Arraez to bat in one of the top two spots in the lineup and produce at a high level, as always.

Killian, 29, led the Giants with eight saves, but his role adjusts with the Phillies, as RHP Jhoan Duran is entrenched as closer. Killian should assume top setup duties in conjunction with LHP Brooks Raley (acquired in a trade this morning from the New York Mets). While Killian's run prevention has been merely average, he should see ample chances for holds. Killian may have more value with the Phillies than he did with the floundering Giants. The Giants may utilize LHP Erik Miller or RHP Keaton Winn in their now-open closer role.

Toronto Blue Jays trade for SP Jose Soriano

Cockcroft (Aug. 3): AL East teams have been making some strange moves as the trade deadline nears. In addition to the Yankees' acquisition of Luis Garcia Jr., who brings to them some roster redundancies, we now have the Blue Jays trading away one starting pitcher only to acquire two within the span of 36 hours. Soriano joins Jameson Taillon as new Blue Jays, though the ex-Los Angeles Angels right-hander is the considerably more relevant one for fantasy purposes.

Soriano's acquisition makes sense in that he's eight years younger and is signed for two more seasons than was Gausman -- Gausman's contract expires at year's end, while Soriano is under team control through 2028 -- so perhaps it's a matter of the Blue Jays deciding to adapt the roster for 2027 while also staying competitive in this year's wild-card race. They're still only 4.5 games back, though they do have five teams ahead of them who are also currently below the cut. We shall see, as the Blue Jays' deadline strategy has something to say about Soriano's fantasy utility over the season's final two months.

For now, assume the Blue Jays maintain their current core. In that case, Soriano joins a team with a significantly better bullpen, as the Blue Jays' relief ERA is more than a half-run better than the Angels' number, though their disappointing lineup has averaged MLB's fewest runs per game (3.92), so run support might still prove a problem. Toronto's Rogers Centre is similarly neutral overall to Los Angeles' Angel Stadium, with a bit more of a home run lean, though Soriano is a ground-ball pitcher for whom that shouldn't prove a big issue.

Soriano's value should stay about the same, though bear in mind that he's not the pitcher who posted an 0.84 ERA across his first seven starts this season. That number is 4.59 over his last 15, so it's probably best to expect something in the 3.50-4.00 range going forward. That's better than a streaming option, but not by a whole lot.

Arjun Nimmala, the Blue Jays' No. 2 prospect in Kiley McDaniel's July update, has dealt with injuries and inconsistency this year but could be a factor for the Angels by 2028. Edward Micheletti and Angel Rivero also went to the Angels in the deal. 

Chicago Cubs trade for SP Kevin Gausman

Cockcroft (Aug. 2): Needing to address their injury-depleted rotation, the Cubs will acquire Gausman, who since the beginning of 2021 has the second-most starts (181), innings pitched (1,053) and fourth-most quality starts (100) in the league. Though never a 15-win (or better) pitcher or top-two finisher in the Cy Young balloting in any of his 13 previous big-league seasons, Gausman has been a plenty reliable starter, both for fantasy and the on-field game.

Gausman is now 35 years old and coming off a shaky stretch that has seen him post a 6.47 ERA in his most recent eight starts, so fantasy managers might understandably hesitate to count on a rebound from him. But he he still generates a good share of swings and misses with his signature splitter, and his 3.33 ERA against sub-.500 teams demonstrates that his worst-case fantasy scenario should be at least that of a matchups pitcher. A drawback to the trade, however, is that the Cubs have one of the game's toughest remaining schedules, so the smart play is to assume that what we've seen from Gausman to this point will probably be his valuation moving forward.

That's still a pitcher who warrants a hefty NL-only bid, if you play in those formats, and a 20-25% of your annual budget bid makes sense if you can't get one of the bigger prizes (Skubal thus far, and we'll see what else transpires before 6 p.m. ET Monday). Gausman is also available in more than 15% of ESPN leagues.

The Blue Jays acquired a pair of prospects, Class-A shortstop Ty Southisene and Triple-A outfielder Brett Bateman, in the deal. Both are players who derive most of their value from their speed, and only Bateman is relatively close to the majors, perhaps with a September cup of coffee or early 2027 ETA.

New York Yankees trade for 2B/1B Luis Garcia Jr.

Cockcroft (Aug. 2): In a bit of a square-peg-in-round-hole move, the Yankees acquired Garcia from the Washington Nationals in exchange for four players. Garcia has been a plenty productive hitter this season, placing fifth among second base and 10th among first base eligibles in ESPN leagues, but his defense at both spots has been historically suspect. The Yankees can certainly use his bat, but they're already well-stocked at any of the three most likely defensive positions where he should slot: First base (Ben Rice/Paul Goldschmidt), designated hitter (Rice and eventually Giancarlo Stanton) and second base (Jazz Chisholm Jr.).

We'll see whether the Yankees have other moves to make, but it's difficult to avoid worry about all of those players' at-bats moving forward. Garcia will almost assuredly become the strong-side first base platoon partner for Goldschmidt, which decreases each of their daily fantasy utility to a degree, and Rice will almost assuredly shift to DH and could become a strong-side platoon partner there once Stanton returns, again costing each player some starts. It's also difficult to look at this deal and not wonder whether the Yankees are worried about how much injured outfielders Aaron Judge and Cody Bellinger might give them the rest of the regular season, and that this is a trade to help bolster the offense wherever they might find it.

At least Yankee Stadium's lefty-friendly confines should help Garcia maintain what has been a career-best power pace. His 23 home runs, 12.6% Barrel and 45.8% hard hit rates are all personal bests, and Yankee Stadium is significantly better for lefty power than Washington's Nationals Park. Garcia will be a matchups must-start when playing home games against righties, and note that he has a career OPS 178 points higher against righties than lefties for his career. So, perhaps he's more of a "roundish-square" peg, but it's still somewhat puzzling considering the Yankees' current roster construct.

Among the four players the Nationals received in return, Jake Bird and Yovanny Cruz have major league experience and can fill roles in what has been a largely wide-open Nationals bullpen, though neither should be added in fantasy leagues until one proves himself over several games. Two pitching-prospect fliers were also included: Jack Cebert, who has put forth a 4.03 ERA and 27.4% strikeout rate across 14 starts and two relief appearances between Class A and Double-A ball, and Ben Grable, who throws hard but is a relief prospect in Double-A. Either could be a factor for the big club a year from now. 

Tampa Bay Rays acquire SP Freddy Peralta

Cockcroft (Aug. 2): A relative disappointment in his four-plus months with the New York Mets, Peralta now joins a Rays organization that is highly regarded for its ability to coax the most out of its pitchers, meaning fantasy owners are probably giddy to hear about the move -- especially those with mountains of FAB resources with which to bid in AL-only leagues. (Yes, you should spend a good chunk of it in those, arguably in the 40%-of-seasonal-budget range.)

While it's true that the Rays do squeeze a lot from their pitchers, especially those joining them on a down note, a closer look at the results show that it's hardly an automatic. Nick Martinez, Zach Eflin and Rich Hill were excellent acquisitions for them, but Steven Matz, Aaron Civale and Luis Patino were unqualified disasters, among more notable pickups they made since the end of the 2020 season. It's dangerous, therefore, to leap to an assumption that Peralta will spring back to his career-best, fifth-in-the-National-League-in-Cy-Young-balloting form from last season, simply because he'll be putting on a Rays uniform. That's a common assumption in the fantasy biz; it's also not the seamless truth people seem to think it is.

Buuuuuut ... the Rays do play in one of baseball's best pitching homes in Tropicana Field, and they have one of the league's better bullpens, with a league-leading 44 saves and a 12th-ranked 3.89 relief ERA, so this is indeed one of the best places Peralta could've possibly landed. If the Rays could coax even a tick of restoration of Peralta's lost fastball velocity, or if they ask him to lean more on his whiff-generating breaking pitches, perhaps he'll come close to his former form. It's certainly worth taking the chance in fantasy leagues, and note that Peralta is still out there as a free agent in nearly 28% of ESPN leagues.

On the Mets side, they acquired three prospects: OF Aidan Smith, SP Gary Gill Hill and 2B Emilen Pitre. None was one of the team's top prospects, with Smith considered the best of the trio but also the furthest from the majors. Hill and/or Pitre could become factors sometime next year, with the latter possessing an intriguing combination of speed and plate discipline.

Peralta's departure, by the way, presents a clearer rest-of-year rotational path for prospect Zac Thornton, and it could increase the chances we'll see additional starts for Jonah Tong. Either might have some streaming value in the right matchup. 

Chicago White Sox trade for SP Luis Castillo

Cockcroft (Aug. 2): The White Sox, still very much a legitimate postseason contender and possessing a three-game lead in the American League Central, acquired much-needed starting pitching help from the Seattle Mariners in Castillo. Though no longer the elite starter he once was -- he was baseball's fifth best-scoring pitcher as recently as 2023 -- Castillo has at least settled into the skill set he now possesses (2 mph less fastball velocity and 10% fewer whiffs with his slider), posting a 4.04 ERA across eight starts and three relief appearances since the Mariners bumped him from their regular rotation and into a piggyback arrangement with their other starters.

Castillo seems to have settled in as a streaming-capable starter, having delivered some of his better starts recently against weaker offenses (CLE, TOR, CIN), and should continue to do so for his new team. The only drawback is that he's leaving arguably baseball's best home pitching environment in Seattle's T-Mobile Park, though Chicago's Rate Field leans slightly pitching-friendly with a similar three-year home run factor (the part of the game that's most concerning for the fly ball-oriented righty).

The Mariners, also a postseason contender but facing more of a climb, received reliever Seranthony Dominguez, who poses almost no threat to closer Andres Munoz's job security and will mainly pad the team's depth. Nolan Jones -- yes, that same Colorado Rockies one-year wonder, now settled as Triple-A depth -- and catching prospect Boston Smith, who has had an excellent year in the minors and is now in Double-A ball, also went Seattle's way. 

Curtis Mead traded from the Nationals to the Red Sox for Connelly Early

Karabell (July 27): Fantasy managers (especially in AL-only formats) enjoyed a weekend gift with the Boston Red Sox acquiring 1B/3B Curtis Mead from the Washington Nationals for LHP Connelly Early. The trade makes sense for both clubs.

The Nationals desperately covet young pitching, and Early -- with a 3.44 ERA and 23.8% strikeout rate in 17 starts -- should join the rotation in the coming weeks when he returns from an IL stint due to elbow inflammation. Even if Early is healthy, fantasy managers may want to be careful in assuming he pitches to prior levels with his new team. The Nationals also have major bullpen issues, for those who selfishly want their starting pitchers to actually win contests.

Mead, however, despite joining his fourth organization in the past two seasons, has been more impactful for fantasy managers and should continue to pile on fantasy points. Mead, 25, ranks among the top 50 hitters in fantasy points this season, yet he is rostered in only 21.3% of ESPN leagues. He is far more valuable in more traditional formats that utilize a corner infield spot. Mead, a right-handed hitter, boasts an .817 OPS versus right-handed pitching, an 11.9% walk rate and a 48.7% pull rate. He should particularly enjoy hitting at Fenway Park.

In addition, the Red Sox figure to employ Mead at second base, which is further great news for fantasy managers, as he will add eligibility there soon (he is currently up to six games at 2B). In typical leagues, multi-position eligibility is critical. We shall see where Mead hits in the lineup for his expected debut Monday night, but it figures to be near the top. After all, 1B Willson Contreras is the lone Red Sox hitter with either a better OPS or more home runs for the season. This trade makes Mead more appealing in fantasy.

headline: Fantasy baseball: Reactions to MLB trade deadline deals
story:
The 2026 MLB trade deadline has now passed, with contending teams (hopefully) wheeling and dealing to get what they needed to add before 6 p.m. ET on Monday. Find out the fantasy baseball implications as a result of the major wheeling and dealing below. 

The biggest domino, of course, fell late Saturday night when the Los Angeles Dodgers acquired Tarik Skubal from the Detroit Tigers. Other big names that ended up not getting moved include Mason Miller, Hunter Goodman and Byron Buxton.

Every season's trade deadline has its own unique set of answers and repercussions. Eric Karabell and Tristan H. Cockcroft have analyzed and provided an outlook for all of the key players on the move, as well as new opportunities that may arise from those left behind now that all the dust has settled.

Note: Not every transaction warranted the attention of fantasy managers, but for those trades that did merit analysis, you'll find them listed below. 

San Diego Padres trade for SP Casey Mize

Cockcroft (Aug. 3): Continuing to fortify their rotation, the Padres picked up a solid arm in Mize, if not the ace-caliber type he was projected to be when he was selected first overall in the 2018 draft. Mize broke through in 2025, his sixth MLB season (fifth when excluding his 2023 wiped out by injury), and he improved his ratios even more this season -- to 2.70 (ERA) and 0.99 (WHIP). That said, his expected ERA was more than a quarter-run higher (3.07), and his fastball has lost a tick-plus off where it was last season, which is a concern for him being able to maintain those numbers.

Fortunately, Mize lands in San Diego's Petco Park, one of the game's most pitcher-friendly environments. He'll see a good number of plus-matchups the rest of the way, so regression probably won't hit him nearly as hard as one might fear, especially if his velocity rebounds in any way. Mize does, by the way, have a 3.23 ERA in seven starts since returning from an adductor injury.

Consider the right-hander to be a potential top-50 fantasy starter on the high end, which isn't a huge stretch considering he's 61st in fantasy points among starting pitchers.

Cleveland Guardians trade for SP Foster Griffin

Karabell (Aug. 3): Griffin, 31, might have been a legitimate contender for NL Rookie of the Year honors with the Nationals, entering his most recent start with a 2.76 ERA and a 1.03 WHIP. Then he allowed six runs at Atlanta last week, and his ERA jumped to 3.06. Even now, the softer-tossing lefty who spent the past three seasons in Japan boasts the 16th-most fantasy points among starting pitchers -- and most pitchers thrive under the tutelage of Cleveland's coaches.

Griffin, who has outpitched his FIP (4.09) all season, remains worthy of a spot in ESPN fantasy leagues, even though he leaves the team leading the big leagues in runs scored to join the team that ranks 29th. Griffin figures to replace fellow LHP Joey Cantillo in the rotation, even though the occasionally tantalizing Cantillo boasts the better strikeout rate and FIP. Griffin offers the rotation more length, though.

Just be careful if Griffin shows signs of struggling in the coming weeks. It may signal that he simply can't overcome his peripherals for an entire season.

New York Yankees trade for OF Heliot Ramos

Cockcroft (Aug. 3): Ramos addresses a serious roster need for the Yankees, whose .284 wOBA and 26.6% strikeout rate from their right-handed hitters since the beginning of June are second- and fourth-worst in the majors. He'll serve as at minimum a left field platoon mate, probably with Spencer Jones moving to right field in place of Jasson Dominguez on those days, but in all likelihood the Yankees regard him a near-regular where Jones and Dominguez will divide up the days on which they sit for him.

Ramos doesn't improve the Yankees' defense at all and, by acquiring both him and Luis Garcia Jr., the team has taken a step backward in that regard, which is a slight concern for their pitchers. It's not enough to change the fantasy values of Cam Schlittler, Max Fried or Gerrit Cole, but if a missed play or three costs any of them a run against their ERA, it shouldn't surprise.

Getting out of Oracle Park, meanwhile, for Yankee Stadium's much more hitter-friendly environment, should help Ramos' overall fantasy appeal. He'll need to raise his fly-ball rate to closer to the 27% mark he had in 2024, rather than the 22% it is this year, but there could be a decent home run stretch in his future, perhaps even enough to double his season total of eight. AL-only managers would do well to place a sneaky claim, in the range of 10% to 15% of seasonal FAB, to secure his services. The best-case scenario could even see Ramos as a clear roster-worthy daily play in standard leagues.

Jones' and Dominguez's values decline with the move, and there's a very real chance that one is headed for the minors if a prolong slump is in their immediate future. After all, the Yankees keep saying that Aaron Judge, Cody Bellinger and Giancarlo Stanton are on the mend, though I see Ramos' and Garcia's acquisitions and seriously doubt that any of that trio will contribute a whole lot over the remaining regular-season games. 

Chicago Cubs trade for SP Clay Holmes

Karabell (Aug. 3): Holmes, 33, last pitched in an MLB game on May 15 when a Spencer Jones line drive broke his fibula. He made numerous rehab starts for the Mets, but his next outing should come in the majors for the Cubs. Don't underestimate Holmes in fantasy. He won 12 games with a 3.53 ERA for last season's Mets, when he was the No. 51 fantasy scorer among starting pitchers.

Even this season, in nine starts, he has managed a 2.39 ERA and a 56% ground ball rate. Only one qualified starting pitcher (Cristopher Sanchez) has a higher ground ball rate. Holmes should thrive for the Cubs. He is rostered in merely 18.8% of ESPN standard leagues, so expect him to become more popular over the coming weeks.

Houston Astros trade for OF Daulton Varsho

Karabell (Aug. 3): Varsho, 30, remains a defensive stalwart in center field. Perhaps that is all the Astros really desire from the former Blue Jay, but he is not having a strong season at the plate. Varsho hit four home runs in April, three in a four-day span. He has homered a mere three times since then and he delivered a sad .205/.241/.241 line in July. He's making more contact than ever, but the lack of power and walks has him barely a top 75 outfielder in ESPN standard points leagues. We have seen Varsho matter more in fantasy. He hit 20 home runs last season. He can steal a base. Perhaps he will improve at the plate while hitting near the bottom of the Astros lineup. Perhaps.

Pittsburgh Pirates trade for RP Luke Weaver

Cockcroft (Aug. 3): Weaver has become one of baseball's better (and more underrated) relievers since joining the New York Yankees in mid-2023, when he worked with Matt Blake to fine-tune his pitch repertoire. Since the beginning of 2024, he ranks 14th in fantasy points accrued in relief -- despite the fact that every pitcher ahead of him on said list has at least 34 more saves than he does over that time. Weaver's 13 regular-season saves, however, as well as the additional four he recorded as the Yankees closer during their 2024 run to the World Series, demonstrate that he has the experience to handle the high-pressure role.

The Pirates have been mixing and matching the ninth this season, with Gregory Soto and Mason Montgomery most recently handling the closer chores, but Weaver is a considerably better fit for the role than either. We'll see whether the Pirates agree, but Weaver has an 0.28 ERA and a 31.1% strikeout rate since the beginning of May, so it shouldn't require much of a competition. Suffice to say, go get Weaver right now in your fantasy leagues if you're in need of saves!

Boston Red Sox trade for C Adley Rutschman

Karabell (Aug. 3): Rutschman, 28, remains on the IL due to left wrist inflammation, but that isn't expected to keep him sidelined much longer. Such is the pressing need the Red Sox have for a front-line catcher. Boston catchers are hitting only .224 with just five home runs this season. Rutschman is batting .251/.331/.433 with eight home runs, though his line is far less impressive since May 1 at .218/.309/.362 with four home runs.

Rutschman draws walks and, that is why, despite missing time with multiple injured list stints, only 10 catcher-eligible options have more ESPN fantasy points. Moving within the division from the Baltimore Orioles to the Red Sox might help with production because it is a better lineup (especially in the past month), but that doesn't guarantee health.

Tampa Bay Rays trade for C/1B/DH Liam Hicks

Karabell (Aug. 3): Hicks, 27, was surprisingly interesting as a rookie for fantasy purposes last season when he played enough and drew enough walks to end up as a top-20 scorer at catcher. He has been much better this season, among the toughest to strike out in baseball, hitting for more power, and Ben Rice is the only catcher with more points. A left-handed hitter, Hicks has not hit left-handed pitching at all, so the Rays might platoon him more than the Marlins were, but that's OK for fantasy if Hicks keeps slugging and walking versus right-handers. This trade should not hurt his fantasy value.

San Diego Padres trade for SP Robbie Ray

Cockcroft (Aug. 3): Ray's 13-year MLB career has had its share of extreme ups and downs -- he won the 2021 AL Cy Young Award and had 433 fantasy points in 2017 but posted a horrendous 6.62 ERA during the COVID-shortened 2020. Still, on the whole, he has been a plenty helpful fantasy option over the years. Even this season, he's on pace for 349 fantasy points, only 21 shy of last year's total despite the fact that his 20.9% strikeout rate is his lowest in any year in which he has pitched at least 30 innings.

Ray's slower fastball velocity -- he's averaging just 93.2 mph with it this year, his lowest in any qualified season since 2019 -- and lightened usage of his slider have a lot to do with the strikeouts decline. Whether either recovers in San Diego is a valid question, but he'll at least maintain a favorable park factor, which is important considering how excellent he was in his home games in similarly favorable pitchers' parks such as Safeco Field in Seattle (3.07 career ERA there) and Oracle Park in San Francisco (3.41) that he once called home.

Ray needs to be in every fantasy lineup for his Petco starts and, though the Padres have a Coors Field series remaining (Sept. 14-17), they play quite a few more road series in pitcher-friendly parks (@NYM, Aug. 17-19; @TB, Aug. 28-30; @SF, Sept. 11-13). He should remain a pretty handy fantasy option -- as he has to this point by ranking 38th in points among starting pitchers.

Cleveland Guardians trade for OF Jo Adell

Karabell (Aug. 3): Adell, 27, hit .239 with 16 home runs for the Los Angeles Angels. He also drew only 16 walks over those four months. This does not typically make for a valuable points-league option, but Adell is the No. 49 outfielder in ESPN standard points formats. That's, well, something. It was better last season when he hit 37 home runs with 33 walks and he was the No. 33 outfielder, though barely a top-100 hitter.

This is what Adell is -- and he offers some value in both real life and fantasy, but the Guardians might not care about the low on-base percentage like fantasy managers do. They need power, and Adell, while not on pace for close to 37 blasts, has more home runs than any current Guardians player. That's telling. Adell is rostered in 33.3% of ESPN leagues. Good for Cleveland, but this trade should not spike Adell's fantasy value.

Seattle Mariners trade for OF/DH Taylor Ward

Cockcroft (Aug. 3): Seeking to beef up an offense that ranks 28th in runs per game for the season (4.02), the Mariners acquired Ward, the No. 29 outfielder in terms of fantasy points scored, from the Baltimore Orioles in exchange for reliever Alex Hoppe and prospects Harrison Kreiling and Brock Moore. Ward should take over as the Mariners' regular right fielder, moving Dominic Canzone to DH and Victor Robles and Rob Refsnyder to the bench.

Ward has been perennially underrated in fantasy leagues over the years, with three seasons of at least 300 fantasy points scored (2022, 2024, 2025), a career-best 368 last season and a pace for 324 this year. Despite that, he has rarely been regarded a locked-in starter in points-league play, though he'll probably remain one in Seattle. The "probably" merely refers to the ballpark change, as going from Baltimore's Camden Yards to Seattle's T-Mobile Park (one of the best pitchers' parks in baseball) represents a downgrade for the outfielder. Nevertheless, it's not enough of one to drop him close to or beneath the roster-worthy line in ESPN standard leagues.

Neither of the prospects is particularly close to being major league ready, nor is either highly regarded. Hoppe, for his part, should help the Orioles as a middle reliever.

Cockcroft (Aug. 2): Needing to address their injury-depleted rotation, the Cubs will acquire Gausman, who since the beginning of 2021 has the second-most starts (181), innings pitched (1,053) and fourth-most quality starts (100) in the league. Though never a 15-win (or better) pitcher or top-two finisher in the Cy Young balloting in any of his 13 previous big-league seasons, Gausman has been a plenty reliable starter, both for fantasy and the on-field game.

Gausman is now 35 years old and coming off a shaky stretch that has seen him post a 6.47 ERA in his most recent eight starts, so fantasy managers might understandably hesitate to count on a rebound from him. But he he still generates a good share of swings and misses with his signature splitter, and his 3.33 ERA against sub-.500 teams demonstrates that his worst-case fantasy scenario should be at least that of a matchups pitcher. A drawback to the trade, however, is that the Cubs have one of the game's toughest remaining schedules, so the smart play is to assume that what we've seen from Gausman to this point will probably be his valuation moving forward.

That's still a pitcher who warrants a hefty NL-only bid, if you play in those formats, and a 20-25% of your annual budget bid makes sense if you can't get one of the bigger prizes (Skubal thus far, and we'll see what else transpires before 6 p.m. ET Monday). Gausman is also available in more than 15% of ESPN leagues.

The Blue Jays acquired a pair of prospects, Class-A shortstop Ty Southisene and Triple-A outfielder Brett Bateman, in the deal. Both are players who derive most of their value from their speed, and only Bateman is relatively close to the majors, perhaps with a September cup of coffee or early 2027 ETA.

New York Yankees trade for 2B/1B Luis Garcia Jr.

Cockcroft (Aug. 2): In a bit of a square-peg-in-round-hole move, the Yankees acquired Garcia from the Washington Nationals in exchange for four players. Garcia has been a plenty productive hitter this season, placing fifth among second base and 10th among first base eligibles in ESPN leagues, but his defense at both spots has been historically suspect. The Yankees can certainly use his bat, but they're already well-stocked at any of the three most likely defensive positions where he should slot: First base (Ben Rice/Paul Goldschmidt), designated hitter (Rice and eventually Giancarlo Stanton) and second base (Jazz Chisholm Jr.).

We'll see whether the Yankees have other moves to make, but it's difficult to avoid worry about all of those players' at-bats moving forward. Garcia will almost assuredly become the strong-side first base platoon partner for Goldschmidt, which decreases each of their daily fantasy utility to a degree, and Rice will almost assuredly shift to DH and could become a strong-side platoon partner there once Stanton returns, again costing each player some starts. It's also difficult to look at this deal and not wonder whether the Yankees are worried about how much injured outfielders Aaron Judge and Cody Bellinger might give them the rest of the regular season, and that this is a trade to help bolster the offense wherever they might find it.

At least Yankee Stadium's lefty-friendly confines should help Garcia maintain what has been a career-best power pace. His 23 home runs, 12.6% Barrel and 45.8% hard hit rates are all personal bests, and Yankee Stadium is significantly better for lefty power than Washington's Nationals Park. Garcia will be a matchups must-start when playing home games against righties, and note that he has a career OPS 178 points higher against righties than lefties for his career. So, perhaps he's more of a "roundish-square" peg, but it's still somewhat puzzling considering the Yankees' current roster construct.

Among the four players the Nationals received in return, Jake Bird and Yovanny Cruz have major league experience and can fill roles in what has been a largely wide-open Nationals bullpen, though neither should be added in fantasy leagues until one proves himself over several games. Two pitching-prospect fliers were also included: Jack Cebert, who has put forth a 4.03 ERA and 27.4% strikeout rate across 14 starts and two relief appearances between Class A and Double-A ball, and Ben Grable, who throws hard but is a relief prospect in Double-A. Either could be a factor for the big club a year from now. 

Tampa Bay Rays acquire SP Freddy Peralta

Cockcroft (Aug. 2): A relative disappointment in his four-plus months with the New York Mets, Peralta now joins a Rays organization that is highly regarded for its ability to coax the most out of its pitchers, meaning fantasy owners are probably giddy to hear about the move -- especially those with mountains of FAB resources with which to bid in AL-only leagues. (Yes, you should spend a good chunk of it in those, arguably in the 40%-of-seasonal-budget range.)

While it's true that the Rays do squeeze a lot from their pitchers, especially those joining them on a down note, a closer look at the results show that it's hardly an automatic. Nick Martinez, Zach Eflin and Rich Hill were excellent acquisitions for them, but Steven Matz, Aaron Civale and Luis Patino were unqualified disasters, among more notable pickups they made since the end of the 2020 season. It's dangerous, therefore, to leap to an assumption that Peralta will spring back to his career-best, fifth-in-the-National-League-in-Cy-Young-balloting form from last season, simply because he'll be putting on a Rays uniform. That's a common assumption in the fantasy biz; it's also not the seamless truth people seem to think it is.

Buuuuuut ... the Rays do play in one of baseball's best pitching homes in Tropicana Field, and they have one of the league's better bullpens, with a league-leading 44 saves and a 12th-ranked 3.89 relief ERA, so this is indeed one of the best places Peralta could've possibly landed. If the Rays could coax even a tick of restoration of Peralta's lost fastball velocity, or if they ask him to lean more on his whiff-generating breaking pitches, perhaps he'll come close to his former form. It's certainly worth taking the chance in fantasy leagues, and note that Peralta is still out there as a free agent in nearly 28% of ESPN leagues.

On the Mets side, they acquired three prospects: OF Aidan Smith, SP Gary Gill Hill and 2B Emilen Pitre. None was one of the team's top prospects, with Smith considered the best of the trio but also the furthest from the majors. Hill and/or Pitre could become factors sometime next year, with the latter possessing an intriguing combination of speed and plate discipline.

Peralta's departure, by the way, presents a clearer rest-of-year rotational path for prospect Zac Thornton, and it could increase the chances we'll see additional starts for Jonah Tong. Either might have some streaming value in the right matchup. 

Chicago White Sox trade for SP Luis Castillo

Cockcroft (Aug. 2): The White Sox, still very much a legitimate postseason contender and possessing a three-game lead in the American League Central, acquired much-needed starting pitching help from the Seattle Mariners in Castillo. Though no longer the elite starter he once was -- he was baseball's fifth best-scoring pitcher as recently as 2023 -- Castillo has at least settled into the skill set he now possesses (2 mph less fastball velocity and 10% fewer whiffs with his slider), posting a 4.04 ERA across eight starts and three relief appearances since the Mariners bumped him from their regular rotation and into a piggyback arrangement with their other starters.

Castillo seems to have settled in as a streaming-capable starter, having delivered some of his better starts recently against weaker offenses (CLE, TOR, CIN), and should continue to do so for his new team. The only drawback is that he's leaving arguably baseball's best home pitching environment in Seattle's T-Mobile Park, though Chicago's Rate Field leans slightly pitching-friendly with a similar three-year home run factor (the part of the game that's most concerning for the fly ball-oriented righty).

The Mariners, also a postseason contender but facing more of a climb, received reliever Seranthony Dominguez, who poses almost no threat to closer Andres Munoz's job security and will mainly pad the team's depth. Nolan Jones -- yes, that same Colorado Rockies one-year wonder, now settled as Triple-A depth -- and catching prospect Boston Smith, who has had an excellent year in the minors and is now in Double-A ball, also went Seattle's way. 

Curtis Mead traded from the Nationals to the Red Sox for Connelly Early

Karabell (July 27): Fantasy managers (especially in AL-only formats) enjoyed a weekend gift with the Boston Red Sox acquiring 1B/3B Curtis Mead from the Washington Nationals for LHP Connelly Early. The trade makes sense for both clubs.

The Nationals desperately covet young pitching, and Early -- with a 3.44 ERA and 23.8% strikeout rate in 17 starts -- should join the rotation in the coming weeks when he returns from an IL stint due to elbow inflammation. Even if Early is healthy, fantasy managers may want to be careful in assuming he pitches to prior levels with his new team. The Nationals also have major bullpen issues, for those who selfishly want their starting pitchers to actually win contests.

Mead, however, despite joining his fourth organization in the past two seasons, has been more impactful for fantasy managers and should continue to pile on fantasy points. Mead, 25, ranks among the top 50 hitters in fantasy points this season, yet he is rostered in only 21.3% of ESPN leagues. He is far more valuable in more traditional formats that utilize a corner infield spot. Mead, a right-handed hitter, boasts an .817 OPS versus right-handed pitching, an 11.9% walk rate and a 48.7% pull rate. He should particularly enjoy hitting at Fenway Park.

In addition, the Red Sox figure to employ Mead at second base, which is further great news for fantasy managers, as he will add eligibility there soon (he is currently up to six games at 2B). In typical leagues, multi-position eligibility is critical. We shall see where Mead hits in the lineup for his expected debut Monday night, but it figures to be near the top. After all, 1B Willson Contreras is the lone Red Sox hitter with either a better OPS or more home runs for the season. This trade makes Mead more appealing in fantasy.

headline: Happ is out of the lineup for Monday's game against the Dodgers.
story: The Cubs will give Happ a breather after he went 0-for-7 with a walk and a strikeout in the final two games of the weekend series with the Yankees. After being recalled from Triple-A Iowa, Kevin Alcantara will enter the starting nine in left field in place of Happ on Monday.

headline: Crews is out of the lineup for Monday's game against the Phillies, Mark Zuckerman of NatsJournal.com reports.
story: Crews will get a breather for the series opener in Philadelphia after he went 3-for-16 with a stolen base, a run and an RBI while starting in Washington's last four games. The Nationals will go with an outfield of Daylen Lile, Jacob Young and James Wood from left to right Monday.

headline: The Red Sox acquired Rutschman (wrist), Jake Rogers and cash from the Orioles on Monday in exchange for catcher Carlos Narvaez, right-handers Anthony Eyanson and Kyson Witherspoon, outfielder Enddy Azocar and a player to be named later, Jake Rill of MLB.com reports.
story: After surging to a 23-3 record over the past 26 games to put itself back in the thick of the playoff race, Boston will shore up one of the few remaining weaknesses on its roster by bringing in a bona fide No. 1 catcher in Rutschman. The 28-year-old backstop has been on the shelf since July 20 due to left wrist inflammation, but he resumed hitting over the weekend and is expected to head out on a rehab assignment during the upcoming week. If all goes well, Rutschman could be ready to make his Boston debut at some point during the team's nine-game, three-city road trip that begins Friday. Before going down with the injury, Rutschman was in the midst of a resurgent 2026 campaign with the Orioles, slashing .251/.331/.433 with eight home runs and a career-low 14.1 percent strikeout rate over 284 plate appearances.

headline: The White Sox acquired Doyle from the Rockies on Monday in exchange for right-hander Mason Adams and infielder Carlos Vielma, Mark Feinsand of MLB.com reports.
story: According to Rosenthal, both teams are reviewing the medicals of all players involved in the deal before completing the trade, but barring any snags, Doyle will head to Chicago, where he should settle in as a fourth outfielder. Since supplying a .763 OPS with 23 home runs and 30 steals in 149 games for the Rockies in 2024, Doyle's offensive production has taken a major step back over the past two seasons while his strikeout rate has climbed. That said, the two-time Gold Glove Award winner still provides strong defense in center field, and his right-handedness will bring more balance to a Chicago outfield that features three left-handed bats in Sam Antonacci, Tristan Peters and Andrew Benintendi.

headline: The Phillies plan to move Harper back to right field to accommodate the arrival of new acquisition Luis Arraez, Todd Zolecki of MLB.com reports.
story: Arraez will remain at second base -- where he's been a plus defender this season -- which will create a domino effect of Bryson Stott shifting to third base, Alec Bohm to first base and Harper back to right field, where he hasn't played since 2022. It means Harper will pick up outfield eligibility in fantasy leagues soon, but the move could also increase his injury risk.

headline: Contreras went 0-for-5 in Sunday's 8-4 win over the Dodgers.
story: Contreras was back in action after missing one game due to a concussion. He's batting .143 (3-for-21) with eight walks and one home run over the last eight contests.

headline: Duran went 1-for-4 with a solo home run in Sunday's 8-4 win over the Dodgers.
story: Duran snapped a 22-game homer drought with a solo shot in the sixth inning. It was the last of the four HRs hit by Boston, which completed a sweep of the Dodgers in Los Angeles. When the Red Sox spiraled in the first half, Duran's name often came up in trade speculation, but the team's recent turnaround makes it buyers heading into Monday's trade deadline. Duran, who entered the All-Star break with a .194 average, clawed his way back to .200 following Sunday's contest (.233 in second half).

headline: Fantasy baseball lineup advice for Monday: Pfaadt an option on slim streaming slate
story:
Check out all of our starting pitcher rankings and other lineup selection tools here to help you make smart fantasy baseball lineup decisions. All fantasy advice is geared toward ESPN 10-team leagues with standard scoring.

Note: All information is accurate as of the time of publication. For updates, as well as any breaking news that might impact today's MLB slate, be sure to check out the latest fantasy baseball buzz. 

Other resources: RP depth chart | Start new league 
ESPN's 2026 Draft Guide | Betting notes for Monday

Pitchers to stream on Monday

  • Putting today's streaming candidates into context, they are the best options on the abbreviated, 10-game Monday slate. By the end of the week, there will likely be at least 30 better options. That said, Brandon Pfaadt is the safest on the docket, but he's not striking anyone out lately, which adds risk to his prognosis. The righty is looking for his third straight quality start, but he has fanned only five over those 13 frames. Limiting home runs is key to Pfaadt's success, and the Arizona Diamondbacks right-hander has yielded only eight long balls in 72 frames this season. He'll open a series in the desert against a San Diego Padres squad that sports league-average power facing right-handers, but Chase Field should suppress it.
  • Prior to his most recent outing, Michael McGreevy logged at least six innings in eight of nine efforts, including six quality starts. Last time out, the St. Louis Cardinals right-hander mustered only 1 2/3 innings, surrendering seven runs on eight hits to the Chicago Cubs. He fanned only 33 in those previous 55 2/3 innings, so he was due for a rough day. McGreevy's lack of dominance is risky, but over the last month, the New York Yankees have been one of the league's least productive offenses at home versus right-handed pitching.

Pitchers to avoid on Monday

  • Michael King was initially set to pitch Saturday, but the San Diego Padres went with Kyle Hart, pushing King to Monday. King has been the subject of trade rumors ahead of the Monday, 6 p.m. ET deadline. This note is more of a warning that he could be dealt before making this start, giving you a zero if he's in your lineup.

Hitters to stream on Monday

  • The Tampa Bay Rays are making their every-other-year visit to Coors Field, where the Colorado Rockies will give the ball to Michael Lorenzen. Most of the Rays' hitters are available in ESPN leagues, with Jonathan Aranda, Cedric Mullins, Chandler Simpson and Victor Mesa Jr. the chief targets against the righty.

headline: Alvarez went 4-for-5 with three doubles, two RBI and a run scored in Sunday's 7-3 win over the Rangers.
story: Alvarez turned in his second four-hit game of the season and recorded his first three-extra-base-hit performance of 2026. His third double came in the seventh inning and drove in two runs to extend Houston's lead. The superstar slugger has now reached base safely in 18 consecutive games and continues to put together an outstanding campaign. Through 111 contests, Alvarez is slashing .330/.442/.650 with 35 home runs, 24 doubles, 84 RBI, 77 runs scored and one stolen base.

headline: Devers went 1-for-3 with a solo home run, an additional run scored and a walk in Sunday's 5-4 loss to the Padres.
story: Devers showed off his opposite-field power with a solo shot to left field in the eighth inning. Over his past 30 games, the 29-year-old has slashed .280/.388/.561 with nine homers, 19 RBI and 22 runs. After a slow start to the season, Devers has found his footing at the plate, posting a .250/.324/.481 slash line with 23 homers, 62 RBI and 60 runs across 112 games in 2026.

headline: Merrill went 2-for-3 with a two-run home run, a stolen base and a walk in Sunday's 5-4 win over the Giants.
story: Merrill took an elevated fastball from Landen Roupp and sent it over the fence in right-center field for a two-run homer to open the scoring in the second inning. The 23-year-old center fielder has flipped a switch at the plate, slashing .302/.333/.534 with eight homers, 21 RBI, 18 runs and five stolen bases over his past 30 games. Overall, he's hitting .237/.289/.398 with 16 homers, 52 RBI, 53 runs and 22 stolen bases across 109 contests.

headline: President of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said that Skubal will make his Dodgers debut Tuesday against the Cubs at Wrigley Field, Jack Harris of the California Post reports.
story: The Dodgers made their acquisition of Skubal official Sunday, with the Tigers receiving three prospects -- outfielders Zyhir Hope and right-handed pitchers River Ryan (hamstring) and Brady Smith -- in exchange for the two-time Cy Young Award winner. Before becoming an unrestricted free agent this summer, the 29-year-old Skubal will headline the Los Angeles rotation over the final two months of the regular season and during the playoffs while the club pursues its third consecutive World Series title. Skubal missed about six and a half weeks earlier this season after requiring a NanoScope surgery to remove a loose body from his left elbow, but he hasn't missed a beat since returning to action June 13. He logged a 2.87 ERA, 0.88 WHIP and 71:8 K:BB over 53.1 innings in his final nine starts with Detroit after coming off the injured list.

headline: Alcantara (12-6) notched win Sunday against the Mets, allowing no runs on four hits and two walks in six innings. He struck out five.
story: That makes it back-to-back scoreless starts for Alcantara, who continues to be a workhorse for the Marlins in 2026. The right-hander has reached the 90-pitch mark in all but two of his 24 outings -- reaching the 100-pitch plateau in half of them -- and he's now thrown at least six innings in six consecutive appearances and 11 of his last 12. Alcantara is set to bring a 3.68 ERA, 1.20 WHIP and 120:41 K:BB over 156.2 frames into a soft home matchup against the Angels.

headline: Lewis went 2-for-4 with a three-run home run in Sunday's 7-6 loss to Seattle.
story: Lewis crushed a three-run homer to center field as part of a five-run eighth inning for Minnesota. The 27-year-old is riding an eight-game hitting streak, though Sunday's two-hit effort was his first multi-hit game during the stretch. In 78 contests this season, Lewis is slashing .221/.300/.406 with 12 homers, 37 RBI, 38 runs and 10 stolen bases.

headline: Raleigh went 1-for-5 with a three-run home run in Sunday's 7-6 win over the Twins.
story: Raleigh crushed an elevated slider for a three-run homer to give the Mariners a 6-0 lead in the seventh inning. He has recorded an RBI in four straight games but has still struggled to find a rhythm at the plate, having not logged a multi-hit effort since June 7. Overall, the catcher is hitting .162/.266/.311 with 12 homers, 43 RBI, 26 runs and two stolen bases across 80 games.

headline: Munoz (5-4) blew the save but picked up the win in Sunday's 7-6 win over Minnesota. He allowed one run on two hits and a walk while striking out two over one inning.
story: Entering with a one-run lead in the ninth inning, Munoz surrendered a game-tying solo homer, though Seattle's offense came through in the bottom of the frame to earn him the win. Sunday marked the 27-year-old's first blown save since June 7, as he has converted 19 of 25 save opportunities in 2026. Overall, Munoz owns a 3.98 ERA, 1.25 WHIP and 63:17 K:BB across 40.2 innings.

headline: Kirby did not factor into the decision Sunday, allowing five hits and a walk over seven scoreless innings against the Twins. He struck out three.
story: Kirby silenced the Twins offense across seven shutout innings, though a bullpen implosion kept him from being credited with the win. It was a much-needed bounce-back effort for the right-hander, who was tagged for seven runs in Monday's loss to the Rangers. Overall, the 28-year-old owns an 8-9 record with a 3.76 ERA, 1.28 WHIP and 110:26 K:BB across 127 innings (21 starts) and is lined up to pitch next weekend against the Rays.

headline: Wheeler didn't factor into the decision in Sunday's rain-shortened outing against the Orioles. He allowed just one hit while striking out three over two innings.
story: While it was a brief day for Wheeler, who didn't return after the first rain delay prior to the third inning, it was still an encouraging showing for the right-hander after he gave up five runs on six hits in just three innings against Miami in his last outing. Overall, Wheeler is 10-2 with a 2.49 ERA, 0.91 WHIP and 126:23 K:BB through 18 starts (105 innings) this season. He's currently lined up to face the Blue Jays at home his next time out, though the Phillies could potentially deploy Wheeler sooner, as he threw just 32 pitches Sunday.

headline: Castillo will make his White Sox debut Thursday in Boston, James Fegan of SoxMachine.com reports.
story: After making his final start for the Mariners on Tuesday before being dealt to the White Sox on Saturday, Castillo will be well-rested and will have some extra time to get acclimated before debuting for his new organization. A three-time All-Star, Castillo brings ample experience to the White Sox rotation, but he submitted a 5.06 ERA and 1.39 WHIP -- both career-worst marks -- over 99.2 innings for the Mariners this season. He's been especially stung by the long ball recently, surrendering seven home runs over his last three outings after giving up just two total in his eight appearances before that.

headline: Sale is slated to make his next start during Atlanta's road series against the Yankees next weekend, Chad Bishop of The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reports.
story: Sale was lined up to toe the rubber in Tuesday's series opener against Miami, but he will now be pushed back a few days. The southpaw has posted a 1.23 ERA and 0.59 WHIP with 31 strikeouts over 22 innings in his last four appearances, so Atlanta's decision to push him back in the pitching schedule isn't performance-based and is likely just a measure to build in some extra rest for him during the grueling season.

headline: Suzuki went 2-for-4 with a double and a run scored in Sunday's 2-1 loss to the Yankees.
story: Suzuki had half of Chicago's four hits and scored the team's lone run in the fourth inning. The outfielder has been dialed in lately, as he's batting .298 over his last 15 games with three home runs, 13 runs scored and 13 RBI. Overall, Suzuki is slashing .273/.364/.476 with 18 long balls, 60 runs and 61 RBI across 95 contests, making him a strong fantasy contributor.

headline: Chapman will undergo another MRI on Monday since his abdominal strain remains bothersome when running, Susan Slusser of the San Francisco Chronicle reports.
story: The 33-year-old isn't believed to have suffered a setback, but he can't quite get over the hump in his recovery. Though manager Tony Vitello said Wednesday that Chapman was expected to come off the injured list during this weekend's series in San Diego, the veteran third baseman will instead be out a bit longer. Christian Koss and Oslevis Basabe have been sharing time at third base lately, and waiver pickup Buddy Kennedy could also factor into the mix for reps at the position while Chapman remains shelved.

headline: Olson went 2-for-4 with a solo home run in Sunday's 4-2 win over the Nationals.
story: Olson tied the game at 2-2 in the fourth inning with a 401-foot blast off Cade Cavalli, his 31st homer this season and his third in his last three games. Since the All-Star break, Olson has gone 17-for-65 (.262) with six homers, putting his slash line at .266/.342/.541 with 69 RBI and 78 runs scored across 491 plate appearances this season.

headline: Iglesias earned the save in Sunday's 4-2 win over Washington, striking out one and walking one in a scoreless ninth inning.
story: Iglesias has now held opponents without an earned run in his last five innings, as he improved to 24-for-26 in save chances this season. The veteran closer's lowered his ERA to 2.25 across 40 innings this year with a 1.05 WHIP and 44:10 K:BB.

headline: Contreras (head) will start at first bae and bat cleanup Sunday against the Dodgers, Chris Cotillo of MassLive.com reports.
story: The veteran slugger was held out of the lineup for Saturday's 3-2 win after being hit in the head by a pitch Friday, but he's good to go for Sunday's series finale in Los Angeles. Contreras will attempt to carry his hot bat into August after closing July with a .323/.488/.629 slash line in 20 games.

headline: Yelich is out of the lineup for Sunday's game against the Angels.
story: Yelich started the previous five games and will get a breather Sunday after going 3-for-19 with three walks, a steal and five strikeouts during that span. Jake Bauers will serve as the designated hitter while Andrew Vaughn starts at first base for the series finale in Anaheim.

headline: Diaz is out of the lineup for Sunday's game against the Rangers.
story: Diaz will get a chance to catch his breath after starting the last three games behind the dish. Christian Vazquez will handle catching duties for Houston in the series finale.

headline: The Rays acquired Peralta from the Mets on Sunday in exchange for outfielder Aidan Smith, second baseman Emilien Pitre and right-hander Gary Gill Hill, Mark Feinsand of MLB.com reports.
story: The right-hander from his scheduled start Friday versus Miami in anticipation of Monday's trade deadline, and the Mets found a willing suitor for his services in the Rays, who pivoted to Peralta after falling short in their pursuit of Tarik Skubal. After being acquired from the Brewers during the offseason, Peralta had a rough time in Queens with a 4.99 ERA, 1.48 WHIP and 113:48 K:BB in 113.2 innings over 22 starts. Tampa Bay amount to a good landing spot for the 30-year-old, given the Rays' track record of getting the best out of their pitchers.

headline: King is no longer scheduled to start Sunday's game against the Giants and will instead make his next turn through the rotation Monday in Arizona.
story: San Diego will have Kyle Hart serve as their opening pitcher in a bullpen game during Sunday's series finale. The Padres didn't provide an explanation behind the late change, but the decision to scratch King adds fuel to the notion that he could be moved ahead of Monday's trade deadline. If the right-hander ends up staying put, he'll tentatively line up for a two-start week, with his second outing coming next weekend at home versus the Astros.

headline: Strider (elbow) appears unlikely to pitch again in 2026, Mark Bowman of MLB.com reports.
story: After landing on the shelf June 13 due to right elbow inflammation, Strider met with Dr. Keith Meister and was prescribed a month of rest. He was expected to be re-evaluated over the All-Star break, but Atlanta hasn't provided a formal update on Strider's progress, and his locker got cleaned out during Atlanta's most recent homestand -- a strong sign that the club isn't expecting the right-hander back over the final two months of the regular season or in the playoffs. Strider labored through eight starts prior to going on the injured list, walking 12.8 percent of the batters he faced while pitching to a 5.31 ERA and 1.36 WHIP across 39 innings.

headline: Perez went 1-for-4 with a solo home run in Saturday's 12-6 loss to the Rockies.
story: Perez followed Jac Caglianone's two-run homer with a solo shot in the third inning as the Royals went back-to-back to build an early 4-0 lead they ultimately couldn't hold. It's been a disappointing campaign overall for the veteran catcher, whose .638 OPS through 104 games would represent a career worst, but he's shown signs of turning things around of late. Since July 1, Perez is slashing .264/.333/.538 with six homers, 16 RBI and 11 runs scored across 24 contests.

headline: Langford went 1-for-5 with a solo home run in Saturday's 5-4 loss to Houston.
story: Langford erased the Astros' early lead in the third inning when he tucked a homer inside the left field foul pole a mere 348 feet from home plate. It was his fourth home run in the last 13 games and 13th of the season.

headline: McLain went 0-for-2 with a walk and a stolen base in Saturday's 4-1 loss to the Pirates.
story: McLain has started three straight games since coming off the injured list, slotting in at second base and hitting ninth in the order. The stolen base was his 12th of the season, and provided a strong sign that the calf injury which landed him on the IL is no longer an issue.

headline: Fantasy baseball fallout from Tarik Skubal's trade to the Dodgers
story:
What does a two-time defending World Series champion -- one with a record-setting, roughly half a billion dollar payroll -- do for an encore?

It trades for the two-time defending Cy Young Award winner from the opposite league, of course.

The Los Angeles Dodgers, perennially committed to investing whatever is necessary to win championships -- and who can blame them for doing so? -- acquired Tarik Skubal from the Detroit Tigers late Saturday night, adding the lefty to their already sound stable of starters that includes No. 6 scoring pitcher Yoshinobu Yamamoto, All-Star Justin Wrobleski and some guy named Shohei Ohtani. They'll also soon get Blake Snell, a two-time Cy Young Award winner himself, and Tyler Glasnow back from the injured list, giving themselves the game's soundest rotation for postseason play.

It's a deal that makes sense for the Dodgers, being that, despite the team's pitching depth on paper, they haven't always extracted the peak results predicted from said arms. Snell has thrown 77 major league pitches and made 12 regular-season starts for the Dodgers between this and last season. Glasnow has made 25 total starts in that time. Roki Sasaki has a 4.59 ERA in two seasons. Ohtani's knee and biceps issues have limited him to designated hitter duty only recently. The Dodgers had a need here, and operating under baseball's current rules construct, they filled it.

Nothing changes for Skubal's fantasy managers, other than those in old-school AL-only leagues that force abandonment of a cross-league traded player. He'll remain one of the three best pitchers in fantasy -- he has been my No. 1 (putting Ohtani's dual eligibility aside for the moment) and will stay so -- dependent upon your opinion of Jacob Misiorowski's durability down the stretch or Cristopher Sanchez's recent inconsistency and hitting-friendly home ballpark.

Open up your FAB wallets, NL-only managers! Skubal is a genuine, spend-the-farm, target for those old-school formats.

The move from Detroit's Comerica Park to Los Angeles' Dodger Stadium drops Skubal in a noticeably more homer-friendly venue, as Statcast's three-year park factors graded the former a 102 (meaning two percent more favorable for homers than a 100-graded, league-average venue) and the latter a major league-leading 126. They're otherwise close in terms of overall environment: 101 for Dodger Stadium and 100 for Comerica Park. Skubal's ERA might take a slight hit, but Dodgers pitchers have performed fine in their home park in recent years, and so should he.

If there's any knock on Skubal's fantasy value going forward, it's what impact the age-old Dodgers "pitching maintenance" strategy has upon his workload. This isn't to say he'll be pulled noticeably earlier from games or have starts skipped, but the nature of Dodgers rotation strategizing is to give Yamamoto and Sasaki extra rest (neither has ever made a U.S. start on fewer than five days' rest ) and to keep the innings and pitch counts in check for their younger starters. There will be times where the schedule or the needs of Skubal's fellow rotation-mates push him back in the order, or a runaway Dodgers National League West title might mean he's minimally utilized in late September during head-to-head fantasy championships.

As for the Tigers, their prospect haul is impressive, led by outfield Zyhir Hope, a top-40 overall preseason prospect, but also including pitching prospects River Ryan and Brady Smith. Hope (fifth) and Ryan (ninth) were the only two placed among Kiley McDaniel's top 10 midseason Dodgers prospects list, but all three should have promising futures. Hope is one of the better dynasty league prospects around, and he's now in a system that is less loaded with outfield competitors as he climbs the ladder.

Ryan is the closest of the three to being major league-ready, though he has a checkered injury history and is currently sidelined with a hamstring injury. It's more likely we'll see him as a competitor for the Tigers' 2027 rotation than this year's, though he could sneak in a few starts with some injury luck in the coming weeks.

headline: Miller (4-1) blew a save but earned the win over the Giants on Saturday, allowing one hit and walking one batter while striking out three over 1.2 innings.
story: Miller was summoned with one out and the bases loaded in the eighth inning to try to protect a two-run lead. He struck out the first batter he faced but then gave up a two-run, game-tying double to Osleivis Basabe. Miller retired the final batter he faced in the frame and also pitched a scoreless ninth, and he emerged with the win after San Diego walked it off in the bottom of the frame. Though he wasn't charged with any runs, Miller was tagged with his first blown save of the campaign in his 29th opportunity. He nonetheless lowered his ERA to a sparkling 0.76 and now has a jaw-dropping 88:16 K:BB across 47.1 innings spanning 45 appearances.

headline: Valdez (6-7) allowed two runs on nine hits and two walks while striking out six over seven innings to earn the win over the Athletics on Saturday.
story: Valdez put together a strong performance in this outing, going seven frames for the second time in his last four starts. The veteran left-hander has allowed 12 runs (11 earned) across 19.2 innings over his last four outings, with his two best performances in that span coming against the A's. He's at a 4.41 ERA, 1.39 WHIP and 98:43 K:BB through 120.1 innings over 22 starts this season. Valdez is projected to make his next start on the road in San Francisco.

headline: Freeman went 3-for-4 with a run scored in Saturday's 3-2 loss to the Red Sox.
story: Freeman has logged three hits in five of the 11 games during his active hitting streak, a stretch in which he's batting .511 (23-for-45). The first baseman had produced only four three-hit performances prior to the end of June. His recent surge at the plate has him batting .310 with an .875 OPS, 15 home runs, 54 RBI, 57 runs scored and five stolen bases over 108 games.

headline: Hernandez went 3-for-4 with a two-run home run in Saturday's 3-2 loss to the Red Sox.
story: Hernandez produced the only scoring play for the Dodgers, taking Payton Tolle deep in the second inning. This was Hernandez's second homer in his last three contests after an 18-game power drought. He has gone 11-for-30 (.367) over his last eight games while maintaining a starting role in the outfield. He's batting .256 with a .736 OPS, 10 homers, 40 RBI, 45 runs scored, 12 doubles and two stolen bases over 76 contests this season.

headline: Acuna went 1-for-4 with a solo home run, an additional run and a walk in an 8-3 win against the Nationals on Saturday.
story: Acuna kicked off the scoring with a 419-foot solo shot to center field in the first inning. It was the star outfielder's second long ball in three games and just his third hit of any sort over six contests since returning from the injured list July 27. Acuna has struggled to a .136 batting average (3-for-22) since his return and has struck out at least once in each game during that span, so he seems to be still shaking off some rust.

headline: Yamamoto (11-7) allowed three runs on four hits and a walk while striking out three over eight innings to take the loss versus the Red Sox on Saturday.
story: Yamamoto has gone seven or more innings in three of his five starts since the beginning of July. He had a little early trouble in this one, giving up solo home runs to Ceddanne Rafaela in the first and third innings before the Red Sox scraped together the decisive run in the eighth. Yamamoto continues to be a workhorse for the Dodgers with a 2.76 ERA, 0.88 WHIP and 121:29 K:BB through 133.2 innings over 20 starts, though he has already given up a career-high 15 homers this year. Yamamoto's next start is projected to be on the road in Arizona.

headline: Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy said after Saturday's 3-2 win over the Dodgers that Contreras (head) is on track to return to the lineup for Sunday's series finale, Tim Healey of The Boston Globe reports.
story: Contreras was struck in the head by a pitch during Friday's series opener. He was removed from that game and was held out of Saturday's lineup as a precaution, but since he's not exhibiting any symptoms of a concussion, Contreras looks poised to start at first base Sunday. Nick Sogard filled in for Contreras on Saturday and went 0-for-2 with a walk.

headline: The Dodgers acquired Skubal from the Tigers on Saturday in exchange for outfielder Zyhir Hope and right-handers River Ryan (hamstring) and Brady Smith, Jeff Passan of ESPN.com reports.
story: Skubal, the biggest domino to fall ahead of Monday's deadline, will head west to the two-time defending World Series champions and form a lethal one-two punch with Yoshinobu Yamamoto atop the rotation. The acquisition of Skubal will give the Dodgers some more stability to the pitching staff while the rotation navigates the absences of Blake Snell (elbow) and Tyler Glasnow (back) along with Shohei Ohtani, who is working solely as a designated hitter while tending to a lingering knee issue. The two-time American League Cy Young Award winner turned in a 2.79 ERA, 0.91 WHIP and 116:14 K:BB over 96.2 innings this season for Detroit.

headline: Carroll went 2-for-5 with a three-run home run, a walk and an additional run scored in Saturday's 12-8 win over the Guardians.
story: Carroll walked and scored in the first inning before launching a three-run blast to break the game open in the seventh. The 25-year-old is batting just .228 through 14 games since the All-Star break, though he's hit safely in 11 of them while tallying eight extra-base hits. For the year, he's slashing .249/.344/.483 with 16 homers, 52 RBI, 67 runs scored and 15 steals across 465 plate appearances.

headline: Fried did not factor into the decision in Saturday's 5-2 loss to the Cubs, allowing one run on two hits and one walk with seven strikeouts over 5.1 innings.
story: Fried allowed a run in the first inning but settled in from there, throwing 54 of 78 pitches for strikes with 12 whiffs before departing in a 1-1 tie. The southpaw has increased his workload in each of his three starts since returning from the injured list July 22, allowing four earned runs over 13.1 innings during that stretch while posting a healthy 18:4 K:BB. He'll take a 3.12 ERA, 0.99 WHIP and 68:23 K:BB across 75 innings this season into a home matchup with Atlanta next weekend.

headline: DeGrom (7-7) took the loss against the Astros on Saturday, allowing five runs on seven hits and five walks with three strikeouts over 3.1 innings.
story: DeGrom was uncharacteristically wild, issuing a season-high five walks while throwing just 52 of 91 pitches for strikes. It was the 38-year-old's shortest outing since a three-inning struggle May 22 in Anaheim, though it's the third time in his past seven starts that he's yielded five or more earned runs. He owns a 3.96 ERA, 1.14 WHIP and 135:29 K:BB across 113.2 innings this season and will aim to rebound in a home matchup with the Orioles next weekend.

headline: Hader earned the save in Saturday's 5-4 win over the Rangers, striking out one in a perfect ninth inning.
story: Hader was summoned to close out a one-run lead in the ninth inning and did so on just 10 pitches. The veteran southpaw remains a perfect 15-for-15 in save chances this season, and he hasn't allowed a hit over his past five outings. On the year, he owns a 1.17 ERA, 0.87 WHIP and 34:10 K:BB across 23 innings while holding opponents scoreless in 22 of 25 appearances.

headline: The Mariners traded Castillo to the White Sox on Saturday in exchange for Seranthony Dominguez, Nolan Jones and Boston Smith, Jeff Passan of ESPN.com reports.
story: The 31-year-old will head to Chicago and give the White Sox another right-hander out of the rotation. Castillo struggled across his four starts in July, going 0-3 with a 5.48 ERA and 1.52 WHIP over 23 innings. That said, the White Sox are hoping to get the version of Castillo that recorded a 3.65 ERA or lower in each of the four seasons prior to 2026, including a 2.99 ERA over 150.1 innings in 2022, when he pitched for both the Reds and Mariners.

headline: Munoz (4-4) picked up the win Saturday in a 4-3 victory over the Twins, giving up a hit and striking out two in a scoreless ninth inning.
story: The closer worked a clean ninth inning in a 3-3 tie and was rewarded for his efforts when Seattle walked it off in the bottom of the frame. It was Munoz's first win since April 22, but he's been plenty effective of late. Over nine appearances and nine innings since the beginning of July, Munoz has produced a 1.00 ERA, 1.00 WHIP and 14:3 K:BB while converting all four of his save chances.

headline: Gilbert didn't factor into the decision in Saturday's 4-3 win over the Twins, giving up three runs on six hits and a walk over seven innings. He struck out six.
story: Solo homers by Luke Keaschall in the fifth inning and Trevor Larnach in the sixth helped cost Gilbert his ninth win of the season, as he squandered an early 3-0 lead and had to settle for his 11th quality start. It's the first time he's served up multiple long balls in a start since June 2, but the right-hander has been tagged with at least three earned runs in five of his last six trips to the mound, leaving him with a 3.86 ERA, 0.96 WHIP and 39:6 K:BB over 39.2 innings during that span. Gilbert will look to get back in the win column in his next outing, which lines up to come at home next weekend against the Rays.

headline: Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said Saturday that Smith (neck) will need at least 3-to-4 weeks to ramp back up to full speed, including a rehab assignment, Katie Woo of The Athletic reports.
story: Smith has been on the Dodgers' injured list since mid-June due to neck inflammation, but he progressed enough in his recovery to resume hitting and throwing in early July. The timeline provided by Roberts means the earliest that Smith will return is late August, and the team expects the veteran catcher to be back before the end of the season. For now, Dalton Rushing will continue to serve as the Dodgers' primary catcher while Eliezer Alfonzo provides depth behind home plate.

headline: Chisholm is starting at second base and batting fifth Saturday against the Cubs.
story: Chisholm exited Thursday's contest against the White Sox after cramping up, and he was held out of Friday's series opener against the Cubs. However, manager Aaron Boone stated ahead of Friday's contest that Chisholm was "fully active," so he was likely just held out because Chicago sent a lefty starter to the mound. All seems to be well with Chisholm given his return to the lineup Saturday.

headline: Chapman (abdomen) will not be activated during San Francisco's weekend series against the Padres, John Shea of the San Francisco Chronicle reports.
story: The Giants were optimistic that Chapman would return sometime this weekend, but the 33-year-old said Saturday that he is still feeling discomfort while running. He's set to be reevaluated Saturday, so an updated timeline for his return could be available in the near future. In the meantime, Christian Koss will continue to serve as San Francisco's primary third baseman.

headline: Contreras, who was hit in the head by a pitch and had to exit Friday's game, isn't in Boston's starting lineup versus the Dodgers on Saturday, Tim Healey of The Boston Globe reports.
story: Contreras initially stayed in the game to run the bases following Friday's plunking, but he was removed on defense in the following frame. He was placed in concussion protocol due to the hit-by-pitch and was reportedly "doing well," per Healey, but he's nonetheless not starting Saturday. In his place, Nick Sogard is in the lineup at first base.

headline: Tucker isn't in the lineup for Saturday's game against Boston, David Vassegh of AM 570 LA Sports reports.
story: Tucker will get a day off to reset after going just 5-for-28 (.179) at the plate while starting the previous nine games. Enrique Hernandez, Andy Pages and Teoscar Hernandez will form the Dodgers' outfield trio while Tucker is on the bench.

headline: Betts isn't in the lineup for Saturday's game against the Red Sox, David Vassegh of AM 570 LA Sports reports.
story: Betts has collected at least one hit in six of his last seven games, but the Dodgers will move him to the bench for the start of Saturday's contest. While he sits, Miguel Rojas will start at shortstop and bat eighth.

headline: Burger isn't in the lineup for Saturday's game against Houston.
story: Burger has notched a base hit in four of his last five games but will grab a seat on the bench to begin Saturday's contest. Joc Pederson will pick up a start at first base as a result, moving Brandon Nimmo into the DH spot and opening up right field for Alejandro Osuna.

headline: Robert isn't in the lineup for Saturday's game against the Marlins, Anthony DiComo of MLB.com reports.
story: Robert will take a day to reset after going just 4-for-33 at the plate in 10 games since returning from the injured list. Tyrone Taylor, A.J. Ewing and Carson Benge will start across the outfield while Robert sits.

headline: Guerrero went 1-for-4 with a double and a run scored in Friday's win over the Cardinals.
story: With the Blue Jays down 1-0, Guerrero led off the sixth inning with a line-drive rocket off the wall in left-center field that left his bat at 112.4 mph. The 27-year-old slugger sat out Wednesday's game due to a sore hamstring, but after Thursday's off day he appears to be fully recovered. It's been a tough campaign for Guerrero, who is stuck in a 14-game homer drought and has just six long balls on the year, but Friday's hard contact offers some hope he might be able to close out the season on a high note.

headline: Schwellenbach (elbow) will likely throw a few more bullpen sessions before being cleared to face live hitters, and he hasn't yet regained his full velocity, Mark Bowman of MLB.com reports.
story: The 26-year-old right-hander has been throwing bullpens, both at Atlanta's spring training complex in Florida and with the big-league club, for a few weeks now, and the team has been mostly pleased with the results. "He looked good," manager Walt Weiss said after Schwellenbach's most recent session Friday. "The ball is coming out good. I've gotten some good reports on him. He's adding to his workload right now. The next step is to face live hitters after throwing about three more bullpens. But he's moving in the right direction and he feels good." While his elbow has held up so far, his velocity isn't yet back at pre-surgery levels, although he has been topping 90 mph in recent outings. If he stays on track, Schwellenbach could begin a rehab assignment in mid-August, and pitching in the majors before the end of the season hasn't been ruled out.

headline: Turner went 3-for-4 with a solo home run and a second run scored in Friday's 6-4 loss to the Orioles.
story: The shortstop took Brandon Young deep in the third inning to break a 2-2 tie, but the Phillies' bullpen wasn't up to the task late. Turner has gone yard in back-to-back games, giving him 16 homers on the season, and through 13 contests since the All-Star break he's delivered a .333/.379/.741 slash line with six home runs, one steal, 10 RBI and 13 runs.

headline: Greene didn't factor into the decision in Friday's 8-7 win over the Pirates, giving up four runs on seven hits and two walks over six innings. He struck out four.
story: A potential pitchers' duel with Paul Skenes never materialized, as the two young righties gave up two runs each in the first inning and wound up getting tagged for three homers and nine runs between them. Greene left the mound after 91 pitches (60 strikes) as he continues to struggle to find his peak form following March elbow surgery, and through five outings and 27.2 innings in July he managed a 6.83 ERA, 1.37 WHIP and 33:9 K:BB. Greene will look to dial things up in his next start, which is set to come at home next week against the A's.

headline: Skenes didn't factor into the decision in Friday's 8-7 loss to the Reds, coughing up five runs on seven hits and four walks over four innings. He struck out seven.
story: The star right-hander managed only one clean inning before getting the hook after 100 pitches (65 strikes), and Skenes served up homers to JJ Bleday in the third inning and Sal Stewart in the fourth while issuing a season high in free passes.
